survivors.title: b-min-sep MC transcripts are sharded by live Rayon thread count: fixed seed gives different epsilon on different hosts
survivors.claim: The OPQ pattern fixed for balls-in-bins by closed issue #331 survives verbatim in the sibling b-min-sep Monte Carlo driver: bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts and bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcripts partition num_samples by rayon::current_num_threads() and seed each chunk StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed + tid) / (seed + 1000 + tid), so the sampled transcript - and the resulting PLD and epsilon - depends on the machine's thread count.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user calibrates a BandMF + b-min-sep run on an 8-core CI box and re-runs accounting with the same seed on a 16-core training host: the reported epsilon differs, golden-value tests flake across runners, and the fixed-seed reproducibility contract (which #550 restored for balls-in-bins with fixed-size seed-indexed shards) is silently broken for this mechanism.
evidence: mc.rs:174-176: 'let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads;' followed by per-tid 'StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64))' (:187) and 'seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)' (:210)

Reproduced with the built extension: _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld([1.0,0.5], 8, 0.05, 1.0, cfg(seed=7)) gives delta_at(1.0) = 0.0073828822922578615 with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, 0.007361131568608619 with 4, 0.007696555912901023 with 8

Contrast with the fixed sibling: balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:46-54 uses fixed-size seed-indexed shards ('deterministic ... regardless of worker count') and has a thread-count-identity Rust test at :549
Not tracked by any open issue (checked issues-open.tsv; #666 covers regression vectors, #683/#688 cover horizon-prefix continuation)
survivors.fix_sketch: Apply the same fix #550 applied to balls-in-bins: split sampling into fixed-size seed-indexed shards (SAMPLES_PER_SHARD) processed with par_chunks_mut and a shard_seed(seed, shard, direction) independent of rayon::current_num_threads(); add a subprocess test mirroring tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py for bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld.

verification.title: b-min-sep MC transcripts are sharded by live Rayon thread count: fixed seed gives different epsilon on different hosts
verification.reasoning: Reproduced directly against the built extension. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:174-176, :187, :210, :255-257 and :364-366 all compute `rayon::current_num_threads().max(1)` and seed each chunk with `seed+tid` / `seed+1000+tid`, so both the transcript corpus (bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts) and the direct warm MC driver draw a different sample set per worker count. Running `_native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld([1.0,0.5], 8, 0.05, 1.0, DiscretizationConfig(discretization=1e-3, seed=7, mc_resolution=0.05))` under RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1/2/4/8 gave delta_at(1.0) = 0.05162982623589127 / 0.051483972011189205 / 0.05213987050718213 / 0.05089388256539482. No ThreadPoolBuilder pins the pool anywhere in the library, so the live host thread count decides. The contrast with the fixed sibling is confirmed: balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:43-55 uses a fixed SAMPLES_PER_SHARD = 1024 with an explicit comment that the shard count must not depend on the worker count, has a Rust identity test at monte_carlo.rs:549, and has a Python subprocess test packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py asserting bit-identical epsilons across RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1/2/8 - there is no b-min-sep analogue. Not a duplicate: open #666 asks for MC regression *vectors* (blocked on #337), and #697 (the b-min-sep prefix/MC-error issue) is closed, so no open issue tracks the thread-count sharding. Severity held at medium rather than raised: each per-host result still carries its own Monte Carlo confidence guarantee, so no privacy bound is violated - what breaks is the documented fixed-seed reproducibility contract (opaque_accounting.pyi:166) that the sibling mechanism explicitly upholds and tests.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user calibrates a BandMF + b-min-sep run with a fixed DiscretizationConfig seed on one host and re-runs the same accounting call on a host with a different core count. Both the cached-transcript path (bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle over a corpus built by bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts) and the cache-miss path (bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld) draw a different sample set, so the reported delta/epsilon changes: measured delta_at(1.0) = 0.0516 at 1 thread vs 0.0509 at 8 threads for the same seed=7. Each value is still a valid MC bound at the configured failure probability, so no guarantee is broken, but fixed-seed reproducibility is lost and any golden-value test for this mechanism would flake across runners - exactly the failure that packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py pins for the sibling mechanism.

survivors.title: Schedule-blind strategy equality lets the composition merge collapse distinct-lr-schedule MF processes
survivors.claim: Residual of closed issue #332: all four MF strategy dataclasses declare lr_schedule as field(default=None, compare=False) (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _lambda_cgd.py:119, _blt.py:132), so MfGaussian.__eq__/__hash__ (plain dataclass semantics comparing the strategy field) are blind to the schedule, while the schedule genuinely changes the strategy's coefficients and priced sensitivity since #529. DpProcess.__or__'s same-leaf merge (opaque-accounting core/_base.py:474-477: 'if left_leaf == right_leaf: return Repeated(left_leaf, left_count + right_count)') therefore collapses two processes differing only in lr_schedule into K repetitions of the LEFT one, silently pricing the second phase at the first phase's schedule.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user composes two MF training phases with identical noise_multiplier/bands/momentum but different lr schedules: mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s1)) | mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s2)) becomes Repeated(phase1, 2); the reported epsilon corresponds to two copies of the s1-weighted sensitivity and can understate the true privacy loss when s2's weighting yields larger sensitivity. The PLD cache is NOT affected (its key materializes the schedule via strategy_cache_key), which makes the eq-path collapse easy to miss in cache-focused tests.
evidence: _band_mf.py:110: 'lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)' inside @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) BandMfStrategy - dataclass semantics exclude compare=False fields from __eq__ and __hash__
_band_mf.py:111-127: coefficients() passes _lr_key(self.lr_schedule, n_steps) into _band_mf_coefficients_cached and sensitivity() is float(coefs.norm()) - the schedule changes the priced sensitivity
core/_base.py:474-477: '__or__' direct merge on 'left_leaf == right_leaf' returning Repeated(left_leaf, ...), discarding the right process object entirely
_mf_gaussian.py:41-75: MfGaussian is a default-eq frozen dataclass whose _pld_cache_key (but not __eq__) goes through strategy_cache_key/materialize_schedule (_schedule_fingerprint.py:12-43)
survivors.fix_sketch: Either include a schedule fingerprint in strategy equality (drop compare=False in favor of a materialization-stable token, or a custom __eq__ comparing _lr_key at the declared horizon), or make DpProcess.__or__'s merge use _pld_cache_key-style resolved identity instead of dataclass __eq__ for leaves that defer resolution.

verification.title: Schedule-blind strategy equality lets the composition merge collapse distinct-lr-schedule MF processes
verification.reasoning: Reproduced end to end, though the reporter's stated mechanism is partly wrong and the real one is worse. `lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)` at _band_mf.py:110 does exclude the schedule from BandMfStrategy.__eq__/__hash__, and MfGaussian (_mf_gaussian.py:41) is a plain frozen dataclass, so two MfGaussian differing only in lr_schedule compare equal (verified: a == b -> True, hash(a) == hash(b) -> True). The reporter's claim that this changes the *priced sensitivity* is REFUTED for BandMF: optimize_toeplitz normalizes, so sensitivity() is 1.0 for every schedule (measured 1.0 for none/linear/cosine/exponential) and the bare MfGaussian PLD is schedule-independent. But the coefficients do change (first coefficient 0.84252 / 0.85096 / 0.85047 / 0.88125 for none/lin/cos/exp at momentum 0.9) and the amplifiers consume the raw coefficient vector, not just the sensitivity (_b_min_sep/__init__.py:170-215 passes `coefs` into the native MC driver). So under amplification the epsilons genuinely differ while the objects still compare equal. Verified: pa = b_min_sep(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, momentum=0.9, lr_schedule=linear)), n_steps=64, p0=0.01) and pb with an exponential schedule give pa == pb -> True, epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.1223865992910398 vs 1.061850795945286. core/_base.py:474-477 then collapses them: pa | pb -> Repeated(pa, 2) and pb | pa -> Repeated(pb, 2), discarding the right operand. Quantified understatement: (pb | pa).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.32408365908405 versus Composed(pb, pa).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.3609055794668186, i.e. epsilon understated by ~2.7%. Genuine residual of closed #332, whose own body names 'DP-FTRL strategies exclude schedules from equality/hash'; PR #675 fixed the PLD cache key via strategy_cache_key/materialize_schedule but left __eq__/__hash__ blind, and no open issue covers the composition-merge consequence. Severity medium rather than high: the trigger requires composing two MF processes differing only in lr_schedule, a real but uncommon two-phase pattern.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user composes two MF training phases with identical noise_multiplier/bands/momentum but different learning-rate schedules under an amplifier, e.g. b_min_sep(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, momentum=0.9, lr_schedule=exp)), n_steps=64, p0=0.01) | b_min_sep(... lr_schedule=linear ...). Because compare=False hides lr_schedule from BandMfStrategy.__eq__, the two processes compare equal and DpProcess.__or__ (core/_base.py:474-477) returns Repeated(left, 2), silently discarding the right phase. The two phases have measurably different epsilon (1.0619 vs 1.1224 at delta=1e-5, because the amplifier consumes the schedule-dependent coefficient vector even though the normalized sensitivity is 1.0 for both), so the merged process reports 1.3241 where the true composition is 1.3609 - a silent ~2.7% epsilon understatement whenever the cheaper phase is on the left. The PLD cache is not implicated: its key materializes the schedule via strategy_cache_key, which is why cache-focused tests do not catch this.

survivors.title: Closed #338 landed no change: asymmetric PLD metrics still renormalize negative-infinity mass away, inconsistently with the symmetric path
survivors.claim: No commit in 79c916e3..4b13d82 changes negative_infinity_mass handling in pld/metrics.rs (git log -S confirms; the closest commits are #466, which only exposes infinity_mass, and #283, docs/labels). The symmetric trade-off pmf_beta floors the Y-CDF with negative_infinity_mass to keep beta conservative (metrics.rs:212-216), while pmf_beta_asymmetric deliberately drops it via clean_probs renormalization (metrics.rs:305 'No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization', :314 'No negative_infinity_mass added') - the exact inconsistency the closed issue title names.
survivors.failure_scenario: beta_at/risk_at on an asymmetric PLD carrying negative_infinity_mass (random_allocation.rs:157-185,250 and connect_the_dots.rs:278 build new_asymmetric PLDs; composition adds the left Chernoff tail budget to negative_infinity_mass in dense.rs) redistributes the -inf mass over the finite grid instead of treating it as mass at -infinity; the resulting beta/risk differs from the conservative symmetric treatment by up to that mass. Magnitude is bounded by the tail budget (~1e-15 analytic default) so practical impact is negligible today, but the guarantee direction is unaudited and the two paths disagree by construction.
evidence: metrics.rs:212-216: symmetric path 'cdf_y[0] = pmf.negative_infinity_mass + pmf.probs[0]' with comment 'keeping beta estimates conservative'
metrics.rs:305: asymmetric path comment 'No negative_infinity_mass: it's absorbed by the renormalization to sum(probs) = 1 - infinity_mass (matching riskcal)'

git log -S negative_infinity_mass 79c916e3..4b13d82 -- packages/opaque-accounting/src/pld returns only #528 (composition-side budgets) and #307 (feature); metrics.rs delta commits are #466 and #283 only
survivors.fix_sketch: Either fold negative_infinity_mass into the asymmetric CDF the same way the symmetric path does (with a derivation of the conservative direction for the symmetrized trade-off), or document the riskcal-matching renormalization as the deliberate resolution with the bounded error recorded; in both cases the closed issue should be reopened or annotated since its titled reconciliation never landed.

verification.title: Closed #338 landed no change: asymmetric PLD metrics still renormalize negative-infinity mass away, inconsistently with the symmetric path
verification.reasoning: The code-level claim is verified verbatim. pld/metrics.rs:211-216 folds negative_infinity_mass into cdf_y[0] in the symmetric pmf_beta with the comment 'keeping beta estimates conservative'. pmf_beta_asymmetric (metrics.rs:276-314) instead runs both PMFs through clean_probs (metrics.rs:126-137), which clamps negatives and rescales the finite mass to sum to 1 - infinity_mass, with comments at :305 and :314 stating that negative_infinity_mass is absorbed by the renormalization and not added. The git evidence holds: git log over 79c916e3..4b13d82 for src/pld/metrics.rs returns only 13c20751 (#466) and f3427abd (#283), neither touching negative_infinity_mass. Two corrections. (1) affects_epsilon is FALSE: pmf_delta (metrics.rs:142-154) and the epsilon inversion read only infinity_mass; negative_infinity_mass never reaches the epsilon path, so only beta_at/risk_at can differ. (2) The magnitude is bounded far more tightly than the report implies. I traced every writer on asymmetric PLDs: random_allocation.rs:172/185 only propagates what its components carry (0 for the Gaussian base), random_allocation.rs:250 sets left_tail_budget = config.tail_mass_truncation/2, and dense.rs:294-312/:360-373 caps the composed value at that budget; tail_mass_truncation defaults to 1e-15 (python/config.rs:29), so the achievable negative_infinity_mass is ~5e-16, below f64 resolution for beta of order 1. geom.rs:406 and :435-436 can move a Pmf's infinity_mass into negative_infinity_mass, but for the Gaussian bases actually used that mass is itself only the right-tail truncation budget. What I could NOT establish is direction: I did not construct a case where dropping the mass makes beta anti-conservative, and the argument cuts both ways (the symmetric inclusion is arguably CDF correctness rather than conservatism; proportional redistribution moves mass to higher losses, lowering beta). PLAUSIBLE for that reason, low severity because the discrepancy is at float-noise magnitude under every default configuration.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: beta_at/risk_at on an asymmetric PLD carrying negative_infinity_mass (built by random_allocation.rs:250 with tail budgets, b_min_sep/mc.rs:318/420, balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:253, or connect_the_dots.rs:278, then self-composed so dense.rs adds the left Chernoff budget) redistributes that mass proportionally over the finite grid via clean_probs instead of anchoring it at the bottom of the CDF as the symmetric path does, so the two implementations disagree by construction. In practice the disagreement is bounded by tail_mass_truncation/2 = 5e-16 at the default configuration - below f64 resolution for a beta of order 1 - and I did not establish that the asymmetric treatment errs in the anti-conservative direction. Epsilon is not affected at all: the delta/epsilon routines read only infinity_mass. The actionable content is an unaudited internal inconsistency between two beta implementations, not a measurable privacy defect.

survivors.title: opaque-accounting wheel-local smoke test imports opaque.dpftrl, breaking the standalone package suite (ARC-006)
survivors.claim: test_repeated_mc_process_preserves_overall_resolution (added by #748 / commit 88a25769) imports opaque.dpftrl.accounting and opaque.dpftrl.noise inside packages/opaque-accounting/tests, but opaque-accounting declares only opaque-base as a dependency (pyproject.toml:13-15) and opaque-dpftrl requires torch - violating ARC-006 (a wheel-local test must be runnable with that wheel's declared dependencies).
survivors.failure_scenario: Running the documented per-package command 'uv run pytest packages/opaque-accounting/tests/' in a torch-free environment (the very configuration the package advertises: 'pip install opaque-accounting alone is torch-free') fails: reproduced in this session - 96 passed, 1 failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.dpftrl'. Full-workspace CI masks it because every lane syncs --all-packages.
evidence: test_smoke.py:146-147: 'import opaque.dpftrl.accounting as ftrl_acc; from opaque.dpftrl.noise import band_mf_strategy'
Session test run: '1 failed, 96 passed' with the dpftrl ModuleNotFoundError as the only failure
packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:13-15: dependencies = ['opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0']
git log -S: introduced by 88a25769 (#748)
survivors.fix_sketch: Move the test to tests/integration/ (the ARC-006 location for cross-capability tests) or rewrite it against a core-only horizon process (e.g. the dpsgd random_allocation behind an importorskip guard, or a stub DpHorizonProcess).

verification.title: opaque-accounting wheel-local smoke test imports opaque.dpftrl, breaking the standalone package suite (ARC-006)
verification.reasoning: Verified statically and reproduced. packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_smoke.py:143-159 defines test_repeated_mc_process_preserves_overall_resolution, whose body does `import opaque.dpftrl.accounting as ftrl_acc` and `from opaque.dpftrl.noise import band_mf_strategy` (lines 146-147) with no pytest.importorskip guard. packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:13-15 declares dependencies = ['opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0'] and the file has no [project.optional-dependencies] at all, so opaque-dpftrl (which pulls opaque-engine and torch) is neither a declared dependency nor an extra of this wheel. It is the only cross-package import in the entire opaque-accounting test directory - I grepped every test file for opaque.dpftrl/dpsgd/engine/optimizers/transformers/patches and torch and got exactly these two lines. Reproduced the failure by installing a meta-path blocker for opaque.dpftrl and running pytest packages/opaque-accounting/tests/: '1 failed, 96 passed', the single failure being ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.dpftrl' in that test - matching the reporter's numbers exactly. This is a clean ARC-006 violation ('a wheel-local test must be runnable with that wheel, its declared dependencies/extras... Tests that intentionally combine independent capabilities belong under tests/integration'), and tests/integration/accounting/ already exists as the correct home. One caveat on the reporter's framing, corrected below: in a repository checkout the documented per-package command would already fail earlier because the root conftest.py:13 imports torch unconditionally, so the torch-free-checkout story is not the real trigger - the contract violation and the dpftrl-absent failure are. Severity low: test placement, not runtime behavior, and full-workspace CI syncs --all-packages so it never fires there. No open issue covers it (#538 is about test-component reuse, not wheel-local dependency scope).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_smoke.py:146-147 imports opaque.dpftrl.accounting and opaque.dpftrl.noise, but opaque-accounting declares only opaque-base as a dependency (pyproject.toml:13-15) and ships no extras, so the test is not runnable with the wheel it lives in - an ARC-006 violation, since a test combining accounting with the DP-FTRL stack belongs under tests/integration/accounting/. Reproduced by making opaque.dpftrl unimportable and running the package's own test directory: 1 failed, 96 passed, with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.dpftrl' as the sole failure. The consequence is scoped to isolated per-wheel test environments and any future dependency-boundary lane; it is invisible in current CI because every lane syncs --all-packages, and in a repository checkout the root conftest.py's unconditional `import torch` (conftest.py:13) would mask it by failing collection first.

survivors.title: Crate duplicates the workspace lint locally instead of opting into [workspace.lints]
survivors.claim: The #422 fix (commit 47aba30e) added a local '[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "warn"' table to the crate rather than '[lints] workspace = true', so the crate still does not inherit the workspace lint table; the root Cargo.toml's [workspace.lints.rust] (lines 13-14) remains applied to zero members.
survivors.failure_scenario: A future lint added to [workspace.lints] in the root Cargo.toml (e.g. escalating unsafe_code to deny, or adding new lints) silently does not apply to opaque-accounting - the only workspace member - recreating the OPQ-134 dead-config situation for every lint except the one that was copied.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/Cargo.toml:39-40: '[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "warn"' (no '[lints] workspace = true' anywhere in the file)
root Cargo.toml:13-14: '[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "warn"' still has no opted-in member
OPQ-134 in the master list prescribed adding '[lints]\nworkspace = true' to packages/opaque-accounting/Cargo.toml
survivors.fix_sketch: Replace the local table with '[lints]\nworkspace = true' in packages/opaque-accounting/Cargo.toml.

verification.title: Crate duplicates the workspace lint locally instead of opting into [workspace.lints]
verification.reasoning: Verified directly. Root Cargo.toml lines 13-14 declare [workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "warn"; packages/opaque-accounting/Cargo.toml ends with a local [lints.rust] unsafe_code = "warn" table and contains no '[lints] workspace = true'. opaque-accounting is the sole workspace member, so the workspace lint table governs zero members and a future lint added there would not reach the only crate. HOWEVER the framing 'the #422 fix was wrong' does not hold: issue #422's own acceptance criteria read 'The crate inherits workspace lints OR declares an equivalent stricter crate-level policy', and the crate-level table satisfies that branch - unsafe_code = "warn" IS live for the crate today. So this is config-hygiene drift-risk, not an unfixed issue and not a regression. One-line change; nowhere near a day of engineering. Not covered by any open tracked issue (parent #325 is closed).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: The `unsafe_code = "warn"` policy is live for opaque-accounting via its own [lints.rust] table, so nothing is currently unlinted. The residual risk is drift only: because no member writes '[lints] workspace = true', the root [workspace.lints] table governs zero crates, so any lint added or escalated there later (or a second workspace member added later) silently fails to apply until someone notices.

survivors.title: b-min-sep MC still thread-count nondeterministic (pattern #331 fixed for balls-in-bins)
survivors.claim: The fix for closed issue #331 (OPQ-182, commit 23c0dbc7) converted balls-in-bins MC to fixed 1024-sample shards, but the sibling b-min-sep Monte Carlo driver in the same crate still partitions by the runtime worker count: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads;` with per-thread RNGs `StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64))` (remove) and `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` (add). The multiset of drawn samples is therefore a function of the host core count / RAYON_NUM_THREADS at a fixed seed, in `bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld` and `bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts` (the transcript registry bakes the thread-dependent draws into the cached corpus). This is exactly the audited defect OPQ-182, which measured an ~11.9% epsilon spread across thread counts for the balls-in-bins twin.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user calibrates sigma for a BandMF + b-min-sep run on a 32-core CI box at seed=42, then re-runs the identical config/seed on an 8-core workstation: the reported epsilon differs at the percent level (OPQ-182 measured 9.06 vs 8.10 for the BnB twin at n=1e5) and the PLD cache/serialized guarantee no longer reproduces. Each individual result is still a valid 1-beta confidence bound (the #748 band holds for any iid draw), so this is a reproducibility/auditability defect on the reported number, not an unsound bound.
evidence: mc.rs:174-176: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads; let remainder = num_samples - samples_per_thread * n_threads;` (prepare path; same pattern at :364-366 in the one-shot driver)
mc.rs:378: `let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64));` - per-thread stream whose sample count depends on n_threads
mc.rs:404: `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` for the add direction - also collides with remove-stream seeds if n_threads > 1000 (theoretical)

grep current_num_threads over the crate returns only these three sites; balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:48 uses the fixed SAMPLES_PER_SHARD scheme with the comment 'The shard count must depend only on the resolved sample count, not on the Rayon worker count'

mc.rs:145-147 docstring documents the thread-layout dependence as the sample-order contract ('thread 0 chunk, then thread 1, ... with the same per-thread StdRng seeds'), i.e., the layout is load-bearing for transcript reuse

Original defect definition: OPQ-182 in docs/development/audit-master-list.md at f398839c^ explicitly notes 'the correlated-strategy path still has it' and prescribes the shard fix later applied only to bnb_mc_pld
No OPEN issue covers this: #697 is about tightening partial-band prefixes and certifying MC statistical error, not machine-dependent sample streams
survivors.fix_sketch: Port the balls-in-bins scheme: partition remove/add sample arrays into fixed SAMPLES_PER_SHARD chunks via par_chunks_mut, seed each shard shard_seed(seed, shard, direction), and derive transcript layout from the shard index rather than tid; extend test_bnb_mc_pld_is_identical_across_thread_counts-style coverage to bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld and the transcript registry (registry corpora must be regenerated or version-tagged since cached layouts change).

verification.title: b-min-sep MC still thread-count nondeterministic (pattern #331 fixed for balls-in-bins)
verification.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. (1) Code: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:173-176 (prepare_transcripts) and :363-366 (one-shot warm driver) both compute `n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1)` and partition num_samples by it, seeding per-thread RNGs `seed+tid` (remove) and `seed+1000+tid` (add) at :187/:210 and :378/:404. The sibling balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:43-48 uses the fixed `SAMPLES_PER_SHARD: usize = 1024` scheme with an explicit comment that shard count must not depend on the Rayon worker count - confirming the #331/PR-550 fix landed only there. (2) Runtime: using the prebuilt extension, `bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld([1.0,0.5,0.25], n_steps=12, p=0.2, sigma=1.5, cfg(seed=42, disc=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-3))` gives delta_at(1.0) = 0.054617 / 0.053409 / 0.051347 / 0.052723 for RAYON_NUM_THREADS = 1/2/4/8 - a ~6% spread at a fixed seed on one host. (3) Reachability: exposed publicly as `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep`, whose _b_min_sep/__init__.py:197,208 calls both native entry points; the transcript registry bakes the thread-dependent draws into the cached corpus. (4) Not tracked: #331 is closed-as-completed for the BnB twin only; #697 (closed; prefix tightness + MC error certification) and open #666 (add MC regression vectors) address different concerns - neither mentions machine-dependent sample streams. Severity stays medium: each individual run remains a valid confidence bound under the #748 band, so this is a reproducibility/auditability defect on the reported number rather than an unsound bound; affects_epsilon kept true, matching how the identical twin #331 was labeled ('impact: epsilon').
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user calibrates or reports epsilon for a BandMF + b-min-sep configuration at a fixed seed on one machine and re-runs the identical config and seed elsewhere (different core count, or RAYON_NUM_THREADS set differently in CI). The Monte Carlo sample multiset differs, so the reported number moves - measured here as delta(eps=1) = 0.0546 vs 0.0513 across 1 and 4 Rayon workers at seed 42, roughly 6%. Cached transcript corpora inherit the same host dependence. Each result is still a valid 1-beta bound, so the guarantee is not unsound; what breaks is reproducibility of the published epsilon and any fixed-seed privacy regression vector for this mechanism.

survivors.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
survivors.claim: After the #341/#528 fixes, one overflow survives: `*c = c.powu(count as u32);` truncates count modulo 2^32. For a multi-element PMF with count > u32::MAX the linear strategy is always rejected (full_result_len > 2^32 > MAX_LINEAR_FFT_SIZE), but when tail budgets are set the circular fallback is taken and the frequency spectrum is raised to the WRONG (wrapped) power, silently composing count mod 2^32 steps instead of count - an epsilon underreport by orders of magnitude. Unreachable from Python: python/pld.rs:31-39 composition_count caps count at u32::MAX with OverflowError. Reachable only via the Rust crate's public self_convolve/self_convolve_with_bounds/Pmf::self_compose API (rlib consumers).
survivors.failure_scenario: A Rust-level consumer (the crate builds as rlib and these functions are pub) calls pmf.with_tail_budgets(1e-15, 1e-15).self_compose(2^32 + 10) on a two-element PMF: the Chernoff window is small, the circular FFT proceeds, and the result is the 10-fold composition presented as the (2^32+10)-fold one, with no error.
evidence: fft.rs:316-318: `for c in a_freq.iter_mut() { *c = c.powu(count as u32); }` - rustfft Complex::powu takes u32; `count as u32` wraps

fft.rs:187-193 checks usize overflow of the result length but a.len()=2, count=2^32+10 gives full_result_len ~ 2^32+11 which fits usize and merely forces the circular branch when allow_circular_fallback is true

python/pld.rs:31-39: `let count = u32::try_from(count).map_err(|_| overflow())?;` - the Python surface is safe, tested by test_singleton_self_convolution_supports_maximum_exponent for the singleton path only
All in-crate call sites (random_allocation.rs:478,671,727; mechanisms/*.rs) pass parameter-bounded counts
survivors.fix_sketch: Guard in self_convolve_with_bounds: `if count > u32::MAX as usize { return Err(...) }` (mirroring the Python boundary), or use repeated squaring of the spectrum with a usize exponent as pow_usize already does for the singleton case.

verification.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
verification.reasoning: Reproduced with a temporary Rust integration test (since removed; tree is clean). `self_convolve_with_bounds(&[0.5,0.5], (1usize<<32)+10, Some((0,15)), true)` returned Ok with values bit-identical to `self_convolve_with_bounds(&[0.5,0.5], 10, Some((0,15)), true)` ([0.0009765625, 0.009765625, 0.043945312, 0.1171875, ...]) - i.e. the frequency spectrum was raised to `count as u32` = 10 instead of 2^32+10, with no error. numerics/fft.rs:316-318 `*c = c.powu(count as u32);` is the wrap. The guards at fft.rs:187-193 catch only usize overflow of the result length, and the strategy selector (fft.rs:195-232) merely routes such a request to the circular branch when a tail budget permits it. Reachability is the limiting factor and keeps this low: python/pld.rs:31-39 caps Pld.self_compose at u32::MAX with an OverflowError, so the Python surface - the only surface Opaque documents - is safe. The wrap is reachable from the crate's rlib API (self_convolve_with_bounds / Pmf::self_compose are pub, crate-type includes rlib), and in principle from Python via random_allocation_gaussian_pld's unbounded `k` (random_allocation.rs:442-447 validates only 1 <= k <= t, and :478 does `single.self_compose(rounds)` with rounds <= k), but that needs k > 4.29e9 participations - a nonsensical input. Not covered by any open issue.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A consumer of the Rust crate calls self_convolve_with_bounds / Pmf::self_compose / Pld::self_compose with count > u32::MAX on a multi-element PMF that has a positive tail-truncation budget (so the circular fallback is allowed) and a narrow output window (so the circular FFT length stays under MAX_LINEAR_FFT_SIZE). Verified: count = 2^32 + 10 silently returns the 10-fold self-convolution, not the (2^32+10)-fold one - an epsilon underreport by orders of magnitude with no error raised. The documented Python API is not affected (u32::try_from guard raises OverflowError); the only Python-side path that could feed an oversized count is random_allocation_gaussian_pld with k > 2^32, which is not a realistic configuration.

survivors.title: Per-group adaptive clip sync permutes group counts across ranks; thresholds silently diverge
survivors.claim: sync_adaptive_clip_state reduces per-group clipped counts positionally by iterating state._num_clipped.items() ('for gname, local_count in state._num_clipped.items(): global_num_clipped[gname] = reduce_scalar(local_count, op="sum")'), but the dict's key order is code-path-dependent: the non-empty stats path (return_aux=False default) stores counts in leaf-traversal group order (engine _compute_clipping_stats builds counts iterating group_norms_dict, packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:500-503, ordered by group first-occurrence along optree paths, _pytree.py:268-283), while the empty-batch path stores dict.fromkeys(initial_clipping_norm.values, 0.0) in PerGroup.values construction order (_adaptive.py:357-360) and the return_aux path uses sorted() order (_adaptive.py:527). When one rank draws an empty batch (routine under Poisson/DDP, guaranteed under RandomAllocationSampler) and PerGroup.values order differs from leaf order (arbitrary user pattern order via per_group()), the positionally-matched all_reduce sums counts of DIFFERENT groups and each rank assigns the sums to differently-ordered keys: global counts are permuted on the empty rank and the recomputed per-group thresholds diverge across ranks with no error. This is closed issue #368's defect class (sync derived from rank-local values, not a schema) surviving in the dpsgd sibling path.
survivors.failure_scenario: Reproduced live (2-rank Gloo): PerGroup(groups={'a_weight':'W','b_bias':'B'}, values={'B':1000.0,'W':1.0}), return_aux=False, rank 0 non-empty (4 examples, all W clipped), rank 1 empty. After sync: rank 0 global counts {'W':4,'B':0} (correct), rank 1 {'B':4,'W':0} (permuted); next thresholds W=1.1008 on rank 0 vs W=0.9013 on rank 1. From then on ranks clip records at different thresholds and scale noise to different max_norms while summing gradients into one model: silent training corruption, and the noise std applied on the low-threshold rank is below the sensitivity actually enforced on the other rank, so released iterates are under-noised relative to the accounted mechanism.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-66 positional reduce_scalar over state._num_clipped.items()
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:357-360 (_empty_num_clipped -> PerGroup.values order), :493/:523 (stats path stores engine dict), :527 (aux path sorted order)
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:500-503 counts dict in group_norms order; _pytree.py:268-283 first-occurrence leaf order
single-process demo: same config yields _num_clipped key order ['W','B'] on a non-empty step and ['B','W'] on an empty step
two-rank Gloo repro output: GLOBAL COUNTS DIVERGED {'W':4.0,'B':0.0} vs {'B':4.0,'W':0.0}; NEXT THRESHOLDS DIVERGED W 1.1008208990097046 vs 0.9012759327888489
existing DDP tests (tests/ddp/dpsgd_ddp_helpers.py:358-470) use identical literal dict order or return_aux=True on all ranks, so the divergence is untested
survivors.fix_sketch: Canonicalize the per-group count dict order at every construction site in _adaptive.py (always build over sorted(current_pg.values.keys()), including _empty_num_clipped and the stats path), and/or make sync_adaptive_clip_state iterate sorted(state._num_clipped) so the collective schedule derives from the schema, not rank-local dict order; add a 2-rank Gloo test with one empty rank and PerGroup.values constructed in non-sorted, non-leaf order.

verification.title: Per-group adaptive clip sync permutes group counts across ranks; thresholds silently diverge
verification.reasoning: The defect is real and I reproduced it end to end, but the reporter's impact claim is wrong, so severity and affects_epsilon are downgraded. CONFIRMED mechanism: (1) _distributed.py:64-66 loops `for gname, local_count in state._num_clipped.items()` and calls reduce_scalar per entry, so the i-th all_reduce is positionally matched across ranks with no key schema. (2) The dict order genuinely differs by code path - _clipped_fun.py:499-503 builds counts from group_norms_dict.items() (leaf first-occurrence order, per _accumulate_group_sq_norms in clipping/_pytree.py:268-283), while the empty-batch path uses dict.fromkeys(clipping_norm.values, 0.0) (_clipped_fun.py:483-484 and _adaptive.py:357-359, i.e. PerGroup.values construction order) and the aux path uses sorted(). Demonstrated in-process: params {aaa_b, zzz_w} with per_group(patterns={'zzz':1.0,'aaa':1000.0}) gives NON-EMPTY key order ['aaa','zzz'] but EMPTY order ['zzz','aaa'], for both return_aux=False and True. (3) Two-rank Gloo run (rank0 non-empty, rank1 empty batch): rank0 global counts {'aaa':0.0,'zzz':4.0} vs rank1 {'zzz':0.0,'aaa':4.0}; next thresholds zzz = 1.1008208990097046 on rank0 vs 0.9012759327888489 on rank1 - matching the reporter's numbers exactly. REFUTED impact: the divergence is NOT silent and never reaches a release. I ran the next step. reduce_pytree (gradients.py:214-217) and reduce_pytree_ (gradients.py:169-171) both call _assert_public_metadata_equal(pytree.max_norm) unconditionally when distributed, which for a PerGroup max_norm runs assert_scalar_equal per group via a min/max all_reduce (_state.py:39-75). Step 2's sum_gradients raised on both ranks: 'RuntimeError: ClippedPytree.max_norm.values[zzz] mismatch across ranks: min=0.9012759327888489, max=1.1008208990097046.' DPTrainer takes the same guarded route (_dp_trainer.py:2100-2103 uses sum_gradients_ on the ClippedPytree), and the error fires before noise_fn, so no under-noised iterate is released and epsilon is unaffected on every advertised path. Residual epsilon exposure exists only if a user hand-reduces grads.pytree instead of the wrapper (bypassing the assert), or if the threshold gap falls under assert_scalar_equal's rtol=1e-5 - in which case the gap is numerically negligible. Severity medium: a supported configuration (per-group adaptive clipping + DDP + Poisson/RandomAllocation empty batches + user pattern order differing from leaf order) aborts at step 2 with an error naming max_norm rather than the real cause in sync_adaptive_clip_state, and the empty rank's per-group clipping-rate metrics are wrong in the meantime. Not covered by any open tracked issue (#368 is closed; #346 concerns the sensitivity-assertion API, not sync key ordering).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: Two-rank DDP with per-group adaptive clipping where the user's per_group() pattern order differs from the model's leaf traversal order (e.g. params {'aaa_b','zzz_w'} with patterns {'zzz':1.0,'aaa':1000.0}), and one rank draws an empty batch (routine under Poisson, guaranteed under RandomAllocationSampler). sync_adaptive_clip_state reduces per-group clipped counts positionally over an order-dependent dict, so the empty rank receives permuted global counts - reproduced: rank0 {'aaa':0.0,'zzz':4.0} vs rank1 {'zzz':0.0,'aaa':4.0} - and the ranks compute different next thresholds (zzz: 1.1008 vs 0.9013). On the following step both ranks clip at their own threshold and sum_gradients / sum_gradients_ aborts training on every rank with 'RuntimeError: ClippedPytree.max_norm.values[...] mismatch across ranks', an error that names the symptom rather than the cause. No under-noised gradient is released: the cross-rank max_norm assertion fires before noise injection on both the library flow and DPTrainer, so the accounted mechanism is not violated. The practical damage is an aborted distributed run with a misleading diagnostic, plus incorrect per-group clipping-rate metrics reported on the empty rank for the intervening step.

survivors.title: AdaClip accounting accepts invalid parameters on direct construction; num_groups=0 silently prices adaptive clipping as free
survivors.claim: The #336/#516 remediation pattern (validate in __post_init__ so direct construction and deserialization cannot pass invalid state to the native call) was applied to Poisson, ParallelPoisson, RandomAllocation and KOutOfT but not to the sibling AdaClip dataclass, which has no __post_init__. Direct construction (or a hand-edited/corrupted serialized process, cf. closed #342 which made every Budget serializable) accepts num_groups=0, negative fraction_noise_std, and negative expected_batch_size. num_groups=0 makes adaclip_sensitivity return z-tilde = z (the K/(4*sigma_b^2) term vanishes), so effective_noise_multiplier equals the bare Gaussian's and the quantile-query privacy cost is charged as zero; negative sigma_b inputs enter squared and are silently accepted.
survivors.failure_scenario: Reproduced: AdaClip(inner=Gaussian(1.1), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=0) yields z_eff=1.1 and poisson(...).pld().epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.14229 vs the correctly-charged 0.14276 — the accountant reports an epsilon omitting the adaptive-clipping release entirely, with no warning. fraction_noise_std=-0.05 and expected_batch_size=-250.0 are likewise accepted (sign lost in the square). A state dict restored with a zeroed num_groups silently under-reports epsilon while the runtime keeps releasing noisy quantile statistics.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/mechanisms/_adaclip.py:23-37 frozen dataclass with no __post_init__; :49-55 effective_noise_multiplier calls _native.adaclip_sensitivity(nm, sigma_b, num_groups) unguarded; :139-156 validation lives only in the adaclip() factory

contrast: Poisson.__post_init__ (_poisson.py:37-61), ParallelPoisson.__post_init__ (_parallel_poisson.py:23-36), RandomAllocation.__post_init__ (_random_allocation.py:67-77), KOutOfT.__post_init__ (_k_out_of_t.py:40-47) all validate for exactly this reason
repro output: 'fns=0.05 ebs=250.0 k=0: z_eff=1.1, eps=0.14229070057507137 <-- ACCEPTED' vs valid config eps=0.14276055192086845; negative fns/ebs also ACCEPTED with unchanged z_eff
survivors.fix_sketch: Add AdaClip.__post_init__ mirroring the factory checks (fraction_noise_std > 0, expected_batch_size > 0, num_groups >= 1 and integral), matching the pattern already applied to the other dpsgd accounting dataclasses; consider the same for Gaussian (negative noise_multiplier currently only fails later inside the native call).

verification.title: AdaClip accounting accepts invalid parameters on direct construction; num_groups=0 silently prices adaptive clipping as free
verification.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _adaclip.py:23-37 is a frozen slots dataclass with no __post_init__; validation exists only in the adaclip() factory (:139-156). Siblings Poisson (_poisson.py:37-61), ParallelPoisson (_parallel_poisson.py:23-36), RandomAllocation (_random_allocation.py:67-77) and KOutOfT (_k_out_of_t.py:40-47) all validate in __post_init__, and _poisson.py carries an explicit comment saying the reason is that direct construction and deserialization bypass the factory. Executed: AdaClip(inner=Gaussian(1.1), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=0).effective_noise_multiplier == 1.1 (bare Gaussian) and poisson(...).pld().epsilon_at(1e-5) == 0.14229070057507137 vs 0.14276055192086845 at num_groups=1 and 0.1441761381215057 at num_groups=4. Also reproduced through the real serialization path: state_dict of a valid num_groups=4 process, edited to num_groups=0, reloads via from_state_dict with no error and reports 0.14229 instead of 0.14418 (~1.3% under). Negative fraction_noise_std=-0.05 and expected_batch_size=-250.0 are accepted and produce the same z_eff as their positive counterparts (sign lost in the sigma_b square). Corrections to the report: negative num_groups does NOT pass silently (-1 and -4 raise OverflowError from the PyO3 unsigned conversion), so 0 is the only fail-open value. Severity lowered from medium to low: every in-repo construction site (_dp_trainer.py:4245, examples/train_sft.py:1821, train_dpo.py:2312, train_dpsgd.py:1568) goes through the validated adaclip() factory, so the under-report requires a caller to supply a nonsensical value or to hand-edit/corrupt a checkpoint, and the magnitude is ~1%. Still genuine and cheap to fix, and it is an anti-conservative (under-charging) silence rather than a fail-closed error. Not a duplicate of open #345 ('Bind AdaClip released statistic to the parameters the accountant charges'): that issue is about the runtime-to-accountant binding of the released quantile statistic, whereas this is a missing constructor-level validator of the #336/#516 normalization family (both closed).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: AdaClip is a public exported type (opaque.dpsgd.accounting.types.AdaClip) and the generic DpProcess codec rebuilds it with cls(**kwargs) on load, so both direct construction and deserialization skip the adaclip() factory's checks. Constructing or restoring AdaClip with num_groups=0 makes _native.adaclip_sensitivity return 1/nm, so effective_noise_multiplier equals the bare Gaussian's and the noisy clipping-fraction release is charged as free: epsilon_at(1e-5) drops from 0.14418 (num_groups=4) to 0.14229 with no warning. fraction_noise_std<0 and expected_batch_size<0 are likewise accepted, silently aliased to their absolute values by the sigma_b square. Negative num_groups does raise (OverflowError from the native u-int conversion), so 0 is the only silently-accepted invalid value.

survivors.title: Sampler RNG streams are exempt from the #728 namespaced-root convention and can collide byte-identically
survivors.claim: Commit 6f6d132a (#728) namespaced every noise-mechanism and auditing RNG stream under a unique string root, and docs/reference/rng.md:208-212 states the convention exists because 'fold_in(key, step) is what every mechanism writes first'. The dpsgd samplers were left out: PoissonSampler seeds numpy directly from key.seed (_poisson.py:108), KOutOfTSampler from self._key.seed (_k_out_of_t.py:58), and RandomAllocationSampler derives each epoch's assignment from the bare integer fold fold_in(self._key, epoch) (_random_allocation.py:125). The documented per-rank Poisson derivation fold_in(key, rank) (_poisson.py:42-49) is byte-identical key material to RandomAllocationSampler's epoch derivation for rank==epoch, and both consume it through the same numpy PCG64 family, so two samplers handed one base key draw correlated (identical) inclusion randomness. Sampler randomness IS the amplification randomness, so a collision correlates subsampling across components with nothing to signal it.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user who trusts the RNG guide's mechanism-root guarantee and reuses one base key for a per-rank PoissonSampler (fold_in(K, rank)) and a RandomAllocationSampler (internally fold_in(K, epoch)) gets rank r's Poisson stream seeded identically to RA epoch r's assignment: the two subsampling processes are deterministically coupled, violating the independence the amplification analyses assume. No shipped example hits this today, so current epsilon values are unaffected; the exposure is the forward-looking class the audit flagged as OPQ-128 and the team fixed for auditing in #374/#728.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:125 'rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)' — bare integer fold, no string root
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:108 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' plus docstring :42-49 recommending fold_in(key, rank)
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:58 'rng = np.random.default_rng(self._key.seed)'
git show 6f6d132a --stat: noise/auditing modules namespaced, no sampler file touched; docs/reference/rng.md:215-222 tag table lists no sampler tags
survivors.fix_sketch: Root each sampler's derivations under a namespaced string (e.g. fold_in(key, 'opaque.dpsgd.random_allocation', epoch)) with a serialization migration note and add the tags to rng.md; alternatively document explicitly that sampler keys are unrooted and must be split from mechanism keys.

verification.title: Sampler RNG streams are exempt from the #728 namespaced-root convention and can collide byte-identically
verification.reasoning: The mechanical facts check out. PoissonSampler seeds numpy from the caller's key verbatim (_poisson.py:108 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)'), KOutOfTSampler likewise (_k_out_of_t.py:58), and RandomAllocationSampler derives each epoch from a bare integer fold (_random_allocation.py:125 'np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)'). No sampler declares a string stream root; packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py enumerates every internal root (paired, dpsgd.gaussian, dpsgd.adaptive_clipping, dpftrl.mf_gaussian, dpftrl.second_moment.*, auditing.*) and no sampler appears, and the tag table at docs/reference/rng.md:215-222 lists no sampler tag. The stated normative convention at rng.md:208-212 ('A mechanism that draws randomness folds one unique string tag into the key it was given') does cover samplers on its face, so the gap is real. Verified numerically that fold_in(K, 3).seed equals the seed RandomAllocationSampler derives internally for epoch 3, and that split(K, 3) == [fold_in(K, i)], so the key material genuinely aliases. Severity kept at low and I deflate the consequence further than the reporter did: the collision surface is sampler-to-sampler only. Namespaced noise mechanisms consume their keys through torch generator_from_key while samplers use numpy PCG64, so even an aliased seed yields uncorrelated numbers across those two families; and a training run uses one sampler, so no shipped or documented configuration hands one base key to two samplers. Also correcting the report's wording: PoissonSampler draws rng.random(n) while RandomAllocationSampler draws rng.integers(0, num_bins, n), so the two are driven by an identical bit stream but the inclusion decisions are coupled, not 'identical'. No open issue covers sampler RNG namespacing (#320 and #356 are about sampler-to-accountant binding, not domain separation), so already_tracked stays 0.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: Samplers are the one family of randomness-drawing components that never fold a namespaced string root into the key they are handed, contrary to the convention published at docs/reference/rng.md:208-212 and enforced for every noise/auditing stream by packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py. Verified aliasing: RandomAllocationSampler(key=K) derives epoch e from fold_in(K, e), which is byte-identical to the key material a user creates with the documented per-rank idiom fold_in(K, rank) for rank==e and to split(K, n)[e]. A caller who hands one base key to two samplers (or hands a sampler a key it also derives sibling keys from) gets deterministically coupled subsampling with nothing to signal it. No current example or documented flow does this, and namespaced noise mechanisms are insulated because they draw through torch generators rather than numpy PCG64, so no shipped epsilon is affected; the item is a hardening/consistency gap, not a live defect.

survivors.title: Accounting now rejects sample_rate=1.0 that the runtime PoissonSampler still supports and tests
survivors.claim: The #336 fix (45f41836) tightened the accounting bound from (0,1] to strictly (0,1): Poisson.__post_init__ raises for sample_rate=1.0. survivors.title: lambda-CGD noise stream is not RNG-namespaced — sibling gap of the #728 stream-root fix
survivors.claim: Commit 6f6d132a (fix(random)!: namespace mechanism RNG stream roots, #728) gave every noise mechanism a namespaced string root (MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD='opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian' in _engine.py:37, GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD in dpsgd), but lambda-CGD's PRNG-replay path was not touched: it still derives per-step torch generators from bare integer folds 'current_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)' (_lambda_cgd.py:280) and 'prev_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step - 1)' (:292). Since split(key, n) is defined as fold_in(key, i), the lambda-CGD noise released at step t is byte-identical to a torch draw from the caller's split(base)[t] key — the exact aliasing the fix eliminated everywhere else, and the exact invariant the new enforcement test states ('Any stream root Opaque derives for itself must be a namespaced string', packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py:1-10). That test cannot catch lambda-CGD because the mechanism declares no root constant at all. docs/reference/rng.md:220 falsely lists 'opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian' as rooting mf_gaussian_noise — untrue when the strategy is LambdaCgdStrategy (the dispatcher special-cases it into _make_lambda_cgd_noise with the raw user key).
survivors.failure_scenario: A user passes key(seed) to mf_gaussian_noise(..., lambda_cgd_strategy(...)) and, following the documented split/fold_in idioms, derives sibling keys from the same base (k0, k1 = split(key(seed)) or fold_in(key(seed), rank)) for any other component that draws torch noise from its handed key. Demonstrated: with lambda_=0.0, the mechanism's step-0 and step-1 released noise vectors are torch.equal to torch.randn drawn from generator_from_key(split(base)[0]) and [1]. Any such correlated second release voids the independent-Gaussian assumption of the lambda-CGD privacy analysis with nothing to signal it; the accountant's epsilon is then not a bound.

survivors.title: BISR runtime keeps n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers, contradicting the documented p-1-vector / PRNG-replay design
survivors.claim: The #360 fix (2507548b) made the BISR runtime operator mathematically exact by handing the DENSE length-n_steps strategy coefficients to inverse_as_streaming_matrix (_bisr.py:200: 'strategy_coefs = _native().bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps)'), whose forward-substitution state is (bands-1, *grad_shape) with bands = len(coef) = n_steps (_toeplitz.py:239-244 'return zero.unsqueeze(0).expand(bands - 1, *zero.shape).clone()'). BISR's whole point is that C^{-1} is banded with p coefficients — the noise row is a p-term convolution of past iid draws computable with p-1 buffers or zero-memory PRNG replay — yet the implementation stores n_steps-1 full gradient copies and does O(n_steps * d) work per step. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md still documents the intended design (':10 Memory: p-1 noise vectors (via PRNG replay or small buffer)', ':96', ':109'). None of that matches the code.
survivors.failure_scenario: Measured on this tree: bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4), n_steps=512, 1M-param model -> streaming state tensor (511, 1000000) = 2.04 GB and 4.27 s per noise step on CPU; both scale linearly in n_steps. A realistic LLM run (n_steps=10k, 1B params) needs ~40 TB of noise state — the mechanism OOMs at any real scale, and at toy scale silently pays O(n_steps) memory/time while the user believes the documented p-1-vector cost. Correctness of released noise is unaffected (operator verified exact).

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_toeplitz.py:239-244 init state = (bands-1, *shape) with bands = coef.shape[0]
Executed: state tensors [(), (511, 1000000)] -> 2.04 GB; one noise step 4.27 s (n=512, d=1e6, p=4)
docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:10,96,109 claim p-1 vectors / PRNG replay
Runtime operator exactness separately verified: materialize() == exact banded C^{-1} (and D*C^{-1} when normalized), max err 0.0 at n=12
survivors.fix_sketch: Apply the banded C^{-1} directly: keep the last p-1 iid draws (ring buffer keyed like the streaming engine's per-step generators, or PRNG-replay them as lambda-CGD does) and emit sum_k inv_c[k] * z_{t-k}, times the column-norm diagonal d_t when normalized. That is O(p) buffers and O(p*d) per step and matches the docs; the current dense forward-substitution path can remain as a cross-check in tests.

survivors.title: lr_schedule is compare=False, so the accountant's structural merge collapses MF mechanisms with different schedules
survivors.claim: All four schedule-carrying strategies declare 'lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)' (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _blt.py:132, _lambda_cgd.py:119). The #332/#362 remediation keyed the PLD caches by materialized schedules (strategy_cache_key), but DpProcess.__or__ merges accountant steps by structural equality (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:460-477: 'if left_leaf == right_leaf: return Repeated(left_leaf, left_count + right_count)'), and dataclass equality ignores compare=False fields. Two per-step DP-FTRL processes that differ only in lr_schedule therefore compare equal and merge, silently pricing every step under the FIRST process's schedule-weighted Gram. Possible overlap with open issue #319 ('Restore DP-FTRL mechanism and strategy invariants'), but this specific residual is a direct leftover of the closed #332/#362 fixes, which repaired cache keys while leaving merge identity schedule-blind.
survivors.failure_scenario: Demonstrated on this tree: pa = per_step(balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5, lr_schedule=cosine)), num_bins=4, n_steps=8)) and pb identical except lr_schedule=constant satisfy pa == pb; pa | pb returns Repeated(count=2) built on pa's leaf, although the two mechanisms' true full-horizon epsilons differ (3.5241 vs 3.6750 at delta=1e-5). A user composing training phases with different LR schedules in one Accountant (acct |= step across phases — the documented idiom) gets an epsilon computed entirely from the first phase's schedule; depending on the schedules the reported epsilon can understate the true cost.

Verified on this tree with lambda-CGD + balls_in_bins(num_bins=4, n_steps=8): the two leaves have true epsilons 3.5374 (cosine) and 3.6750 (constant) at delta=1e-5, yet compare equal and merge. A user who composes a cosine-schedule phase then a constant-schedule phase in one accountant is charged entirely at the cosine price, understating the cost. A strategy with no schedule at all also compares equal to one with a schedule.

survivors.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice the docs claim is fully accounted
survivors.claim: The #350 fix removes the data-dependent skip, but the replacement pattern feeds the raw, un-noised private statistic stats.all_finite into LossScaler.update (docs/user-guide/precision.md:99, _loss_scaler.py:185-195), so the scale at step t+1 is a function of private data at step t that was never released or accounted. The scale changes which per-example gradients overflow and are zeroed by clip_pytree's sanitization (_pytree.py:520-527), so under add/remove adjacency one record's presence at step t can flip the scale at t+1 and thereby change other records' released contributions at t+1 by up to C each - per-step sensitivity conditioned on a shared transcript is no longer C, and per-step PLD composition (which allows adaptivity only through released outputs) does not strictly cover the composed mechanism. docs/user-guide/precision.md:102-106 asserts the overflow path is fully 'composed into the accountant'; the pre-fix warning that this is 'not free privacy-wise' was deleted in 18f67eac.
survivors.failure_scenario: fp16 functional-API training following the documented recipe (loss_scaler + return_stats + accountant). After neighboring datasets diverge in a single overflow event, the backoff (or delayed growth) makes the two runs use different scales on all subsequent steps; examples whose scaled gradients sit near the fp16 overflow boundary are zeroed in one run and kept in the other, changing the released noisy gradients by more than the accounted sensitivity C while the reported epsilon is unchanged.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/precision/_loss_scaler.py:185-195 - update(state, grads_were_finite) consumes the raw finiteness bit and moves scale by growth/backoff factors

docs/user-guide/precision.md:99 'scaler_state = scaler.update(scaler_state, stats.all_finite)' and :102-106 'the zero contribution is still noised, optimized, and composed into the accountant. The stats then back off the next loss scale.'
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:520-527 - non-finite leaves are zeroed, making the released contribution scale-dependent exactly when overflow flips
git show 18f67eac - deleted 'A skip is data-dependent and is not free privacy-wise. Unless separately analyzed, advance accounting on a public fixed schedule.'
survivors.fix_sketch: Either drive the scale schedule from a released (noised) overflow statistic or a public schedule, or document that stats.all_finite-driven scaling is an adaptive query outside the stated guarantee and quantify/gate it the way adaptive clipping is gated for MF mechanisms.

verification.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice the docs claim is fully accounted
verification.reasoning: Every link checked in source. (1) ClippingStats.all_finite (_clipped_fun.py:73, computed by _all_finite at :98 and aggregated at :439-442/:481) is the raw, un-noised finiteness bit over the batch's pre-clipping per-example gradients - explicitly documented at _clipped_grad.py:165-169 as 'measured after pre_clipping_transform and before clipping sanitizes NaN/Inf'. (2) LossScaler.update (_loss_scaler.py:185-195) consumes that raw bit and multiplies the scale by backoff_factor / growth_factor, so scale_{t+1} = f(private data at step t). (3) clip_pytree (_pytree.py:520-527) nan_to_num's non-finite per-example gradients to zero before clipping, so which records contribute at all is a function of the scale. Hence under add-or-remove adjacency a single record's presence at step t can flip the scale from t+1 on, and with a different scale a different set of records is zeroed, so the released sums for the two neighbouring runs differ by more than the accounted C. That adaptivity flows through a private bit, not through a released output, so per-step PLD composition does not cover it. (4) The docs push exactly this wiring (precision.md:99) and now describe the overflow path as fully 'noised, optimized, and composed into the accountant' (:102-106); 18f67eac deleted the prior 'A skip is data-dependent and is not free privacy-wise' warning and the module docstring's remaining caveat only forbids suppressing the update, not the scale feedback. docs/limitations.md's 'Telemetry outside the guarantee' says to keep such statistics private but says nothing about feeding them back into training. Severity medium, not high: the loss scaler is an opt-in functional-API recipe (DPTrainer does not use it - grep for loss_scaler in opaque-transformers/src is empty), the channel is one bit per step reaching the adversary only indirectly through subsequent releases, and I did not construct a numeric attack. Open issues #383/#322 are alignment/transformers-scoped release-boundary umbrellas and do not cover the engine loss scaler.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: fp16 functional training following docs/user-guide/precision.md: the raw pre-clipping bit stats.all_finite is fed straight into scaler.update, so the loss scale at step t+1 is a function of private data at step t that was never noised or accounted. Because clip_pytree zeroes non-finite per-example gradients, the scale decides which records contribute; two neighbouring datasets that diverge on one overflow event therefore run every subsequent step at different scales and can differ in more than one record's clipped contribution, breaking the per-step sensitivity C that the PLD composition assumes. Reported epsilon is unchanged and is therefore an under-estimate of the composed mechanism. The docs assert the overflow path is fully composed into the accountant and the previous data-dependence warning was removed in 18f67eac.

survivors.title: The #352 wrapper-blindness pattern survives in unscale_grads and global_norm (silent no-op / silent 0.0 on ClippedPytree)
survivors.claim: Issue #352 was fixed only for all_finite. Its siblings still treat DP wrapper types as opaque leaves: LossScaler.unscale_grads uses bare optree tree_map (_loss_scaler.py:172-183 via opaque.pytree.tree_map, pytree.py:126-142), and ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree are unregistered dataclasses, so unscale_grads(ClippedPytree, state) returns the wrapper object unchanged without unscaling anything - empirically confirmed (returned object is the input, leaf value 8.0 unchanged with scale=4). Likewise opaque.pytree.global_norm(ClippedPytree) silently returns 0.0 because tree_leaves finds no tensor leaves - empirically confirmed (0.0 vs 5.0 on the unwrapped pytree).
survivors.failure_scenario: A user following the torch.amp.GradScaler mental model calls scaler.unscale_grads on the ClippedPytree returned by grad_fn (instead of wiring it as pre_clipping_transform): the call silently no-ops, gradients remain grads of the scaled loss clipped at C (clipping rate ~100%, silently wrong training configuration). A user logging global_norm(clipped_grads) gets a constant 0.0 and debugs the wrong thing. Neither path raises.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/precision/_loss_scaler.py:172-183 - unscale_grads uses tree_map; wrappers are leaves and fail the isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) test
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:122-123, 142 - tree_leaves/tree_map are bare optree; ClippedPytree is not registered as a pytree node
empirical: unscale_grads(clipped({'g': tensor([8.0])}, max_norm=1.0), state) with scale=4 returns the same object with 8.0 intact; global_norm(clipped({'g': [3,4]}, max_norm=1.0)) == 0.0
survivors.fix_sketch: Mirror the all_finite fix: have unscale_grads and global_norm unwrap ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree/SecondMomentClippingOutput (unscale should also rescale max_norm metadata, or raise TypeError directing the caller to .pytree, as ClippedPytree.__add__ already does for unsupported ops).

survivors.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure, breaking step-shape stability under Poisson sampling
survivors.claim: _empty_batch_response builds zero gradients with zero_grads_like(args, argnums) (_clipped_grad.py:218, _helpers.py:76-86), which copies the parameter pytree's structure and dtype, while non-empty steps return gradients in the configured output dtype and in whatever structure pre_clipping_transform produces (documented as allowed to change structure, _clipped_grad.py:170-175). Empirically confirmed on the current tree: with dtype=torch.float32 and bf16 params, a non-empty batch returns fp32 and an empty batch returns bf16; with a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform, a non-empty batch returns a dict and an empty batch returns a bare Tensor. adaptive_clipped_grad's own empty-batch path (_adaptive.py:402-415) has the same behavior, and auto_clipped_grad inherits it.
survivors.failure_scenario: Poisson sampling routinely produces empty batches; the empty-batch path exists precisely so those steps look like every other step. A run configured with dtype= or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform gets a differently-shaped/typed ClippedPytree on empty steps: MF noise (which latches metadata on first call) or torchopt optimizer state initialized from a non-empty step then errors or silently casts when an empty step arrives - and if the FIRST step is empty, everything downstream latches the wrong template.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:216-230 - zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple); no dtype cast, no pre_clipping_transform application
empirical: dtype=torch.float32, bf16 params -> non-empty dtype torch.float32, empty dtype torch.bfloat16; pre_clipping_transform=lambda g: {'g': g} -> non-empty structure dict, empty structure Tensor
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:402-415 - same zero_grads_like short-circuit
survivors.fix_sketch: In the empty-batch path, apply pre_clipping_transform to the zero pytree and cast leaves to the configured output dtype, in clipped_grad, adaptive_clipped_grad, and auto_clipped_grad alike; or reject structure-changing transforms/dtype overrides at factory time when they cannot be honored on empty batches.

verification.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure, breaking step-shape stability under Poisson sampling
verification.reasoning: Reproduced both halves. _empty_batch_response (_clipped_grad.py:216-256) builds the zero gradient with zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple) (_helpers.py:76-86 = tree_map(torch.zeros_like, params)), which copies the parameter pytree's structure and dtype and applies neither the configured output dtype nor pre_clipping_transform. Executed: bf16 params with dtype=torch.float32 give torch.float32 on a non-empty batch and torch.bfloat16 on an empty one; pre_clipping_transform=lambda g: {'q': g['w']} gives keys ['q'] on a non-empty batch and ['w'] on an empty one. I also traced the downstream consequence: MF noise built on the transformed template raises ValueError('dictionary key mismatch...') on the empty step, while gaussian_noise silently accepts the wrong structure and emits a noised pytree with the wrong keys. adaptive_clipped_grad repeats the same short-circuit at _adaptive.py:402-415. No test pins empty-batch dtype or structure (test_clipped_grad.py's empty-batch tests only check zeros/stats). Severity low: it needs one of two optional knobs (dtype= or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform) together with an empty Poisson batch, the structure case fails loudly under MF noise, and nothing about sensitivity or noise scale changes, so epsilon is unaffected.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: With dtype= set or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform, empty Poisson batches return a ClippedPytree whose dtype/structure differs from every non-empty step. Verified: dtype=torch.float32 with bf16 params -> fp32 on non-empty steps, bf16 on empty ones; pre_clipping_transform renaming 'w'->'q' -> keys ['q'] non-empty, ['w'] empty. Downstream, MF noise whose state was built from the transformed template raises ValueError on the empty step, and gaussian_noise silently returns a noised pytree keyed by the untransformed names, which then mismatches optimizer state. adaptive_clipped_grad and auto_clipped_grad share the same short-circuit.

survivors.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
survivors.claim: The #368 empty-batch fix left the aux schema itself data-dependent under per-group clipping: the empty-batch short-circuit hardcodes clipping_rate=0.0 while the non-empty per-group path emits clipping_rate=None, so _sync_clipping_rate's new presence check raises RuntimeError on every rank the first time some-but-not-all ranks draw an empty Poisson batch.
survivors.failure_scenario: DPTrainer with TrainingArguments.clipping_norm={...} (per-group dict; fixed and adaptive modes both affected) + DDP + Poisson sampling. On a step where one rank's Poisson draw is empty and another's is not, sync(aux) in training_step (_dp_trainer.py:2104) raises 'Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.' on every rank and the training run dies mid-stream. Reproduced live on 2-rank gloo: rank 0 empty -> clipping_rate=0.0, rank 1 batch of 4 -> clipping_rate=None, both ranks raise (no hang — follow-up collective still works — so it is a fail-closed crash, not silent corruption).
evidence: _clipped_grad.py:238 (empty-batch aux): 'clipping_rate=0.0,' — unconditional, even when clipping_norm is a PerGroup

_clipped_fun.py:852-856 (non-empty aux): 'clipping_rate=(stats.clipping_rate if isinstance(stats.clipping_rate, float) or stats.clipping_rate is None else None)' — per-group rates are a dict, so the aux field becomes None

engine/clipping/_distributed.py:224-230: 'local_presence = int(clipping_rate is not None); ... if min_presence != max_presence: raise RuntimeError("Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.")'
dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:423 empty path 'clipping_rate=0.0' vs :617 non-empty 'clipping_rate=aux.clipping_rate if aux is not None else None' — adaptive per-group has the same divergence
Reachability: _dp_trainer.py:1408-1421 builds a PerGroup clip_norm from the documented clipping_norm dict; :4177-4185 passes it to clipped_grad(return_aux=True); :2099-2104 calls sync under DDP

Live 2-rank gloo repro output: 'rank 0: local clipping_rate=0.0 bs=0 / rank 1: local clipping_rate=None bs=4 / both ranks: SYNC RAISED RuntimeError: Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.'

The shipped regression test _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group (engine_ddp_helpers.py:673-715) hand-builds the non-empty rank with clipping_rate=0.5 (a float), which real per-group clipped_grad never produces — the test passes while the real path crashes
survivors.fix_sketch: Make aux clipping_rate presence a function of the clipping schema, not the batch: in _empty_batch_response (and the adaptive empty path) emit clipping_rate=None when clipping_norm is a PerGroup (matching the non-empty aux), or have _sync_clipping_rate derive presence from the clip configuration. Extend _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group to build both auxes through the real clipped_grad(PerGroup, return_aux=True) instead of hand-crafting fields.

verification.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
verification.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Single-process check with clipped_grad(clipping_norm=PerGroup(...), return_aux=True): a batch of 4 yields aux.clipping_rate=None (because _compute_clipping_stats returns a per-group dict at _clipped_fun.py:499-510 and the aux constructor at _clipped_fun.py:849-856 collapses any non-float, non-None rate to None), while a batch of 0 takes the short-circuit at _clipped_grad.py:238 and yields aux.clipping_rate=0.0. No open issue covers it (#368 is the closed fix that introduced the presence check).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainer with a per-group TrainingArguments.clipping_norm dict (fixed or adaptive mode) under DDP with Poisson sampling. On any step where at least one rank draws an empty batch and at least one does not, the empty rank reports clipping_rate=0.0 while every non-empty rank reports None (per-group rates are a dict and are collapsed to None by the aux constructor). _sync_clipping_rate's min/max presence collective then disagrees and raises RuntimeError('Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.') on every rank, aborting the run mid-training. Verified live on 2-rank gloo; the process group is left usable (follow-up collectives succeed), so this is a fail-closed crash, not silent corruption or a hang.

survivors.title: Distributed CI lane passes silently if its test selection collapses to zero
survivors.claim: The blocking two-rank lane added for #366/#328 sets allow-empty-test-selection:true, and the runner converts pytest exit code 5 (no tests collected) into success per package, so a refactor that renames/unmarks the 'distributed' tests or moves them out of the scanned package paths turns the desync-regression lane green with zero tests executed.
survivors.failure_scenario: A marker rename (e.g. 'distributed' -> 'ddp'), a conftest change that deselects the ddp directories, or moving the spawn tests out of packages/*/tests makes every suite in the linux-distributed job exit 5; run_python_test_package.sh logs '::notice::No tests matched' and exits 0; the branch-protection 'Python tests' gate sees success. The exact regression class this lane exists to block (OPQ-001-style collective desync) can then reland invisibly — the failure mode the original audit called out for OPQ-051.
evidence: .github/workflows/pr.yml:76-85: python-tests-distributed passes 'allow-empty-test-selection: true' with pytest-marker 'distributed and not cuda' (same in ci.yml:41-50 and prepare-release-implementation.yml:307-317)
.github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:40-43: 'if [[ "$status" -eq 5 && "$ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION" == "true" ]]; then echo "::notice::No tests matched..."; exit 0; fi'
No step in python-tests.yml asserts that at least one suite in the distributed job actually collected tests (TEST_RESULTS_FILE is written but never checked for non-emptiness)
survivors.fix_sketch: For the distributed lane, require a minimum collected-test count: either drop allow-empty-test-selection and give every package at least one distributed test, or add a post-loop check that TEST_RESULTS_FILE is non-empty for the suites known to carry distributed tests (engine, dpsgd, dpftrl, optimizers, alignment, transformers).
