survivors.title: Optimizer-state drift audit marshals float64 fingerprints through float32 collectives with rtol=1e-5
survivors.claim: Residual of #365: _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal computes (sum, sumsq, min, max) in double precision but compares them via assert_scalar_equal without compute_dtype, so the collective runs at the float32 default with atol=1e-8/rtol=1e-5 — cross-rank optimizer-state drift below roughly 1e-5 relative (or below float32 resolution for large sums, ~2^-24 relative) passes an audit whose stated purpose is exactly drift detection.
survivors.failure_scenario: Two ranks' Adam second-moment tensors diverge by a small relative amount (e.g. a non-deterministic kernel introduces 1e-6-relative drift that compounds over thousands of steps). sync_optimizer_state fingerprints each tensor, but min/max reduction of the float64 stats happens in float32 and the isclose check uses rtol=1e-5, so the audit stays silent while parameters slowly de-synchronize.
evidence: optimizers/distributed.py:98-103: 't = tensor.detach().double(); assert_scalar_equal(float(t.sum().item()), name=...)' — no compute_dtype argument on any of the five calls

engine/distributed/_state.py:65: 'dtype = compute_dtype or torch.float32' and :174: tensor dtype 'compute_dtype or torch.float32' — the float path defaults to float32 marshalling with atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5

The module's own docstring (optimizers/distributed.py:85-93) says the fingerprint exists because 'drift detection is the entire point'; the master-list OPQ-049 note said float32 marshalling 'partially defeats' the audit — the integer half was fixed by #365 (ints now exact int64), the float half was not
survivors.fix_sketch: Pass compute_dtype=torch.float64 and atol=0.0/rtol=0.0 (or a deliberately tiny tolerance) on the five assert_scalar_equal calls in _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal, mirroring what sync_object's assert_equal path already does for float fields.

verification.title: Optimizer-state drift audit marshals float64 fingerprints through float32 collectives with rtol=1e-5
verification.reasoning: Code path verified and reproduced. optimizers/distributed.py:97-102 casts each tensor to double() then hands the four stats to assert_scalar_equal with no compute_dtype; engine/distributed/_state.py:57-70 and :171-181 marshal the float through a torch.float32 collective tensor and compare with torch.isclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5) in float32. Ran a 2-rank gloo repro of _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal: a uniform 1e-6 relative drift on a 1000-element float32 tensor PASSED undetected on both ranks; 1e-3 was correctly caught. The audit catches gross desync but is blind below ~1e-5 relative, and the double() precision is computed then discarded. One correction to the reporter's framing: the dominant limitation is the rtol=1e-5 default, not the float32 marshalling -- passing compute_dtype=torch.float64 alone would still not detect 1e-6 drift, so a fix must tighten atol/rtol too. Severity low: debug/audit facility only; no privacy or numerical guarantee depends on it, and a real desync would normally exceed 1e-5. No open issue covers it (#365 was the closed integer-half fix; #321 is closed).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: Under DDP, sync_optimizer_state fingerprints each optimizer-state tensor in float64 but compares the four statistics through a float32 collective with torch.isclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5). Verified on 2-rank gloo: a uniform 1e-6 relative difference between two ranks' state tensors passes the audit silently, while 1e-3 is caught. Cross-rank optimizer-state drift below roughly 1e-5 relative therefore goes unreported by an audit whose stated purpose (module docstring, optimizers/distributed.py:85-93) is drift detection; the binding constraint is the rtol default, with float32 marshalling as a secondary ceiling (~1e-7 relative for large sums).

survivors.title: DPTrainer never consults ScheduleFreeState.x: schedule-free eval and checkpoints use the wrong weight sequence

survivors.title: Adafactor module docstring misstates the BC default (says True, actual False) plus two stale/incorrect memory statements
survivors.claim: Three docstring statements contradict the code: (1) lines 30-31 say noise_bias_correction 'defaults to ``True`` so BC is on by default' while the signature (line 303) is noise_bias_correction: bool = False and the arg docstring (line 335) correctly says False -- the module contradicts itself; (2) line 28 says the phi-EMA is subtracted 'with a positive floor', stale since the where-fallback semantics that b9faed0a documented in _bias_correction.py:20-31 (torch.where(corr>0, corr, v), no floor, _adafactor.py:238-239); (3) lines 6-7 say rank<2 tensors 'fall back to a scalar second moment' while _init_v_for_leaf:120 allocates torch.zeros_like(leaf) -- a full per-element tensor for vectors (paper-correct behavior, wrong description; also relevant to closed #406's memory-doc alignment).
survivors.failure_scenario: A DP user reads the module doc (the file whose header sells the BC feature), concludes bias correction is already active, and trains with adafactor() defaults: the second-moment factors silently retain the +sigma^2 noise bias the docstring told them was being removed. No error, just the uncorrected optimizer the docs say they are not running.
evidence: _adafactor.py:30-31: '``noise_bias_correction=True`` activates this path; defaults to ``True`` so BC is on by default.'
_adafactor.py:303: 'noise_bias_correction: bool = False' and :335: 'Defaults to ``False``; Adafactor's relative-step per-tensor normalization already plays BC's role'
_adafactor.py:238-239: 'torch.where(corr_row > 0, corr_row, new_v_row)' -- fallback, not a positive floor
_adafactor.py:120: 'return (torch.zeros_like(leaf),)' for leaf.dim() < 2 -- per-element, not scalar
survivors.fix_sketch: Rewrite the three sentences: default is False; subtraction falls back to the uncorrected factor where non-positive (cross-reference _bias_correction.py); rank<2 leaves keep a full per-element second moment (unfactored), matching the paper.

verification.title: Adafactor module docstring misstates the BC default (says True, actual False) plus two stale/incorrect memory statements
verification.reasoning: All three sub-claims checked against the exact lines. (1) _adafactor.py:30-31 reads 'noise_bias_correction=True activates this path; defaults to True so BC is on by default', while the signature at :303 is 'noise_bias_correction: bool = False' and the argument docstring at :335-338 correctly says 'Defaults to False' -- the file contradicts itself and the module header is the misleading half. (2) :28 says the phi-EMA is subtracted 'with a positive floor', but :238-239 is torch.where(corr_row > 0, corr_row, new_v_row): when the correction goes non-positive the code falls back to the UNcorrected EMA, materially different from clamping to a small positive floor. (3) :5-7 say rank<2 tensors 'fall back to a scalar second moment' and the helper docstring at :106 repeats 'or scalar', but _init_v_for_leaf:120 returns (torch.zeros_like(leaf),) -- a full per-element second moment for vectors. The code is paper-correct (Shazeer and Stern keep full v for non-matrix tensors); the prose is wrong and overstates the memory saving. Docs-only, severity low, no epsilon impact. Nothing open covers it (#406 is closed).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reads the _adafactor module header -- the section that sells the DP noise-variance bias correction -- concludes from lines 30-31 that noise_bias_correction defaults to True, and trains with adafactor() defaults. The actual default is False (:303), so the row/column second-moment EMAs silently retain the +sigma^2 DP noise bias the header claims is removed. Two secondary prose errors compound the confusion: line 28 describes the correction as subtracting the phi-EMA 'with a positive floor' when the implementation (:238-239) instead falls back to the uncorrected EMA via torch.where, and lines 5-7 claim rank<2 tensors use a scalar second moment when _init_v_for_leaf:120 allocates a full per-element tensor, overstating the memory saving.

survivors.claim: _scale_by_adadelta accepts bc_floor (line 121) and adadelta() computes and passes bc_floor = eps*eps (lines 377, 382), but the scaler body never reads it (zero uses between lines 122-304; the noisy_squared_grads branch clamps at min=0.0 on line 247 instead). Commit b9faed0a removed the identical dead parameter from _adagrad.py and rewrote _bias_correction.py:31-34 to say bc_floor 'belongs to the private second-moment branch' of the optimizers that have it -- Adadelta has that branch and does not use bc_floor there, so both the parameter and that doc claim are misleading for this optimizer.

_adadelta.py:377 'bc_floor = eps * eps' and :382 'bc_floor=bc_floor,'
_adadelta.py:247 'v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)' -- the substitution branch's actual guard

verification.title: Dead bc_floor parameter left in Adadelta after the same cleanup removed it from Adagrad
verification.reasoning: Verified by reading and grep. packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_adadelta.py:121 declares 'bc_floor: float,' in _scale_by_adadelta's signature; :377 computes 'bc_floor = eps * eps' and :382 passes it. A grep for bc_floor across the whole file returns exactly those three hits -- the scaler body never reads it. The private second-moment branch instead guards with 'v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)' (a min=0 clamp, not an eps^2 floor), relying on the additive eps inside _rms for denominator safety. By contrast _rmsprop.py:124 and _adam.py:193 genuinely apply '.clamp(min=bc_floor)' in their noisy_squared_grads branches, and _adagrad.py has no bc_floor at all after b9faed0a. The secondary claim about _bias_correction.py:31-34 is weaker than stated: that text reads 'The separate bc_floor clamp seen in some optimizers belongs to the private second-moment branch' -- hedged with 'some optimizers', so it is not literally false, only unhelpful next to Adadelta's live bc_floor plumbing. #405 (the cleanup issue) is closed; no open issue covers this.

A maintainer auditing Adadelta's noisy_squared_grads branch sees adadelta() compute bc_floor = eps*eps and pass it into _scale_by_adadelta, and assumes an eps^2 denominator floor is applied there as it is in RMSprop (_rmsprop.py:124) and Adam (_adam.py:193). survivors.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token alignment term (and thus disagrees with TRL)
survivors.claim: With DPOConfig(use_weighting=True), opaque's WPO pair weight is exp(mean masked per_token_logps) while both the cited WPO paper (arXiv:2406.11827, Eq. 2) and TRL 1.12 subtract the per-token alignment term log(sum_v p(v)^2) before averaging; the trainer multiplies per-example losses by this wrong weight, so WPO runs optimize a different objective than the paper the docstring claims to implement. The repo knows: test_trl_parity.py:518-526 marks the parity test as strict xfail instead of fixing the weight. Possibly inside the umbrella of OPEN issue #323 ('align trainer and alignment behavior with their public contracts'), but no open issue names WPO specifically.
survivors.failure_scenario: User sets use_weighting=True (WPO) on DPOTrainer expecting the published WPO objective / TRL-equivalent behavior. _dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 multiplies each pair's loss by _wpo_weight(chosen)*_wpo_weight(rejected) built from raw per-token logps; TRL computes aligned_logps = per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2x) - 2*logsumexp(x)) first (site-packages/trl/trainer/dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606). Since log(sum p^2) is in [-log V, 0] and varies per token, the two weights differ systematically, silently changing training dynamics and results versus the cited method.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_wpo.py:62-67 — 'avg_logp = (per_token_logps * mask).to(acc_dtype).sum(dim=-1); avg_logp = avg_logp / token_count...; return avg_logp.detach().exp()' — no logits, no alignment term.

packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518-526 — '@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=("wpo_weights omits the WPO weight-alignment term log(sum_v p_v^2) that both TRL and the authors' reference implementation apply; the fix needs the logits, so it changes the public signature"))'.

installed trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 — 'lse2 = torch.logsumexp(2.0 * shift_logits, dim=-1); log_denom = lse2 - 2.0 * lse1; aligned_logps = (per_token_logps - log_denom) * shift_completion_mask; ... weights = torch.exp(mean_logps)'.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 applies the product of the two opaque weights to the per-example loss; _wpo_weight already receives chosen_out.logits, so the logits needed for the fix are available at that call site.
survivors.fix_sketch: Add an optional logits (or log_denom) argument to wpo_weights and average (per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2*logits,-1) - 2*logsumexp(logits,-1))) under no_grad, mirroring TRL; wire _dpo_trainer._wpo_weight to pass the logits it already has; flip the xfail into a passing parity test. The weight stays detached and per-example, so DP clipping semantics are unchanged.

verification.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token alignment term (and thus disagrees with TRL)
verification.reasoning: Every link verified. (1) Implementation: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_wpo.py:63-67 computes avg_logp = sum(masked per_token_logps)/token_count and returns avg_logp.detach().exp() -- it takes no logits and applies no alignment term. (2) Paper: I fetched the arXiv HTML of 2406.11827 and the adopted 'sampled alignment' weight (Eq. 2) is w(x,y) = exp( (1/|y|) sum_t log [ pi(y_t|x,y_<t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v|x,y_<t)^2 ] ), and the paper states 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO due to its superior performance.' So the sum_v p_v^2 denominator IS part of the adopted formula. (5) The repo knows: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518-526 is a strict xfail naming exactly this omission; I ran it and it xfails as documented. Documentation claims the paper: _wpo.py's module docstring cites arXiv:2406.11827 and docs/reference/alignment.md:70 lists 'wpo_weights() -- per-example WPO weight (arXiv:2406.11827)'. Not tracked: both plausible umbrellas, #323 and #475, are CLOSED (2026-08-27), and a targeted issue search for WPO/use_weighting returned nothing. Severity medium, not high: use_weighting is opt-in, the deviation is a per-example reweighting of the loss with no privacy consequence (the weight is detached and per-example, so per-record sensitivity is unchanged), and the divergence is already pinned by a strict xfail -- but it is a silent, undocumented-to-users departure from the cited objective.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets DPOConfig(use_weighting=True) expecting the published WPO objective (and TRL-equivalent behavior). opaque's weight is exp(mean_t log p(y_t)); the paper's Eq. 2 and TRL both use exp(mean_t [log p(y_t) - log sum_v p(v)^2]). Since log sum_v p(v)^2 lies in [-log|V|, 0] and varies per token and per example, the two weights differ by a per-example factor exp(-mean_t log sum_v p_v^2) > 1 that is not constant across the batch, so relative pair weighting -- and hence training dynamics and results -- differ systematically from the cited method. No error, no warning; only a strict xfail in test_trl_parity.py records the gap.

survivors.title: Chat-template transform: overstated coverage comments and exact-string generation-marker guards
survivors.claim: Residuals around the #387 fix (all fail-closed, none silently wrong): (a) the Strategy-2 comment 'Handles ChatML, Llama-3, Phi-3, etc.' (line 229) and the _wrap_gemma_shared_expression docstring 'Gemma 2/3 templates' (line 376) overstate coverage — the real Llama-3-Instruct template, canonical shared-expression ChatML, and the real Gemma-3 text template all raise ValueError (Gemma-3 because its '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' expression matches the \bcontent\b regex, making content_matches count 2 and aborting at line 405); (b) both the idempotency check (line 214, '_GEN_START in template') and apply_chat_template_with_mask's guard (_completion_mask.py:84, exact "{% generation %}" substring) miss whitespace-control marker variants ('{%- generation -%}') that transformers itself accepts via regex, so a valid pre-marked template is either rejected outright or gets a second nested marker pair (verified: nesting yields duplicated identical spans, so the final mask is still correct).
survivors.failure_scenario: SFTTrainer with completion_only_loss on chat data and a Llama-3/ChatML/Gemma-3 tokenizer raises ValueError at dataset prep despite comments suggesting support; a user who hand-installed '{%- generation -%}' markers (valid per transformers' r"\{\%-?\s*generation\s*-?\%\}" check) gets a ValueError from apply_chat_template_with_mask telling them to install markers they already have. Training either stops with a confusing error or proceeds correctly after redundant re-wrapping — no wrong mask is ever produced.
evidence: Probe run against real templates: GEMMA2 spans ['<start_of_turn>model\nASSIST1<end_of_turn>\n', ...] correct; GEMMA3, CHATML (shared-expression), LLAMA3 all 'ValueError (fail-closed)'; QWEN25 correct.

_chat_template.py:403-406 — content_pat matches both "{{ message['content'] | trim }}" and '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' in the real Gemma-3 template (probe printed both), so len(content_matches) != 1 returns None.

_completion_mask.py:84 — 'if not active_template or "{% generation %}" not in active_template: raise ValueError' vs transformers 5.16.1 chat_template_utils: 'if return_assistant_tokens_mask and not re.search(r"\{\%-?\s*generation\s*-?\%\}", chat_template)'.

Probe: get_training_chat_template on a template already containing '{%- generation -%}' returned a nested '{%- generation -%}{% generation %}...{% endgeneration %}{%- endgeneration -%}' template; rendered indices [(26, 41), (26, 41)] — duplicated but identical spans.
survivors.fix_sketch: Use the same whitespace-tolerant regex as transformers for both the idempotency check and the _completion_mask guard; fix the Strategy-2 comment to name templates it actually handles (role-branched templates, Phi-3) and drop 'Gemma 3' from the helper docstring, or exclude raise_exception(...) expressions from content_pat so real Gemma-3 works.

verification.title: Chat-template transform: overstated coverage comments and exact-string generation-marker guards
verification.reasoning: Reproduced all three sub-claims against real templates downloaded from the Hub. (a) Running get_training_chat_template on the real Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct template (NousResearch mirror), the real gemma-3-1b-it template (unsloth mirror), and the canonical shared-expression ChatML template all raise ValueError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'); gemma-2-2b-it and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct succeed. So the Strategy-2 comment 'Handles ChatML, Llama-3, Phi-3, etc.' (_chat_template.py:229) and the _wrap_gemma_shared_expression docstring 'Gemma 2/3 templates' (:376-380) overstate coverage. The Gemma-3 mechanism is exactly as reported: content_pat = re.compile(r"\{\{-?\s*[^}]*\bcontent\b[^}]*-?\}\}") finds 2 matches in the real Gemma-3 template -- "{{ message['content'] | trim }}" and '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}' -- so the len(content_matches) != 1 check at :403-406 returns None. survivors.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO Eq.(2) weight-alignment term that TRL and the paper apply
survivors.claim: wpo_weights computes exp(mean masked per-token logp) only, while WPO Eq.(2) (arXiv:2406.11827) and TRL's use_weighting additionally subtract the per-token log-sum of squared token probabilities (verified in installed trl 1.12.0 DPOTrainer source: 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper ... lse1 = logsumexp(shift_logits); lse2 = logsumexp(2.0 * shift_logits); log_denom = lse2 - 2.0 * lse1'). The module docstring (:3-22) and docs/alignment/trainers.md:283-285 present the shipped weighting as the paper's method without caveat. The divergence was exposed by the #380/#431 parity work and xfail'ed (packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518) instead of fixed or documented user-facing.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user migrating a TRL DPO run with use_weighting=True gets systematically different per-example weights, so training dynamics and results silently diverge from both TRL and the cited paper while the docs claim equivalence. Utility only — the weight is detached and per-example, so per-example DP is unaffected. May nominally overlap open umbrella issues #323/#475, but neither names this concrete divergence, discovered after they were filed.

trl 1.12.0 DPOTrainer inspected in-session: computes lse2 - 2*lse1 correction under 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper'
test_trl_parity.py:518 xfail reason: 'wpo_weights omits the WPO weight-alignment term log(sum_v p_v^2)'; pytest run: 1 xfailed
docs/alignment/trainers.md:283-285 documents use_weighting as arXiv:2406.11827 without caveat
survivors.fix_sketch: Extend wpo_weights to accept the logits (or a precomputed per-token log-denominator) and apply Eq.(2)'s log(sum_v p_v^2) term, or document in _wpo.py and docs/alignment/trainers.md that opaque implements a simplified sequence-probability weight that differs from TRL/the paper.

verification.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO Eq.(2) weight-alignment term that TRL and the paper apply
verification.reasoning: Verified against the primary source, not just TRL. Extracted the WPO paper PDF (arXiv:2406.11827): Section 3.2 defines the unnumbered length-normalized weight w = exp((1/|y|) sum_t log pi(y_t|x,y<t)); Section 3.3 'Weight Alignment' then defines greedy and 'sampled' alignment, and it is the sampled-alignment form w = exp((1/|y|) sum_t log [pi(y_t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v)^2]) that carries equation number (2), followed by 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO'; Algorithm 1 says 'Calculate the alignment weight via Eq. (2)'. So Eq. (2) is the aligned weight and opaque implements only the Section-3.2 precursor. _wpo.py:33-46 returns (masked logp sum / count).detach().exp() with no logits and no alignment term; the trainer path is no better: _dpo_trainer.py:1251-1267 builds per-token logps from logits and forwards them to wpo_weights, and :1138-1144 multiplies the loss by chosen*rejected. Installed trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 computes log_denom = lse2 - 2*lse1 = log(sum_v p_v^2) under the comment 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper'. The divergence is not proportional (log sum_v p_v^2 varies with per-token confidence), so relative weighting across examples differs. test_trl_parity.py:518 pins it with a strict xfail; _wpo.py:3-22 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:281-284 present the shipped weighting as arXiv:2406.11827 without caveat. Utility only (weight is detached, per-example), so affects_epsilon false. Not a duplicate: the umbrellas #323 and #475 are both closed on GitHub (2026-08-27) and neither body mentions WPO or use_weighting.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets DPOConfig(use_weighting=True) - advertised in docs/alignment/trainers.md as WPO (arXiv:2406.11827) and in _wpo.py's docstring as the paper's weighting. Opaque applies exp(mean masked log p_t), the paper's Section-3.2 precursor weight, while both the paper's default (Eq. (2), sampled alignment) and TRL's use_weighting apply exp(mean [log p_t - log sum_v p_v^2]). Per-example weights, the relative weighting across the batch, and the resulting training dynamics differ systematically from TRL and from the cited method, with no user-facing caveat; only a strict xfail in the internal parity suite records the gap. No privacy impact.

survivors.title: Sliding-window constraint silently dropped under SDPA when attention_mask is None
survivors.claim: The #397 fix's vmap_create_causal_mask returns None (SDPA is_causal skip) whenever attention_mask is None, attn_impl != 'eager' and no cache is populated, with no sliding-window awareness; vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask propagates that None ('if causal_mask is None: return None'), so SDPA falls back to plain causal attention and the look-back limit is silently discarded whenever the window binds (seq_len >= sliding_window). Upstream explicitly refuses this skip: transformers/masking_utils.py:262-263 returns False from _ignore_causal_mask_sdpa when 'local_attention_size is not None and kv_length >= local_attention_size'.
survivors.failure_scenario: Any patched sliding-window model (Mistral/Ministral with sliding_window set, Gemma2, Gemma3 text with default sliding_window=512, Cohere2, Phi-3) called with attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default) and no attention_mask — the standard model(input_ids) pattern in eval/perplexity/generation-prefill code — attends to the full context on sliding layers. Empirically: tiny Mistral, sliding_window=4, seq=12, SDPA: upstream logits identical with and without mask (diff 0.0); the patched model deviates by max-abs 0.39 without a mask while matching upstream exactly (0.0) with one. DPTrainer flows are unaffected because the collators always emit attention_mask (opaque-alignment _language_modeling.py:133-173).

All TestSlidingWindowCausalMask tests use _attn_implementation='eager' (tests/transformers/runtime/test_masking.py:114-135), so the SDPA branch is untested

verification.title: Sliding-window constraint silently dropped under SDPA when attention_mask is None
verification.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. masking.py:76-82 returns None whenever attention_mask is None, _attn_implementation != 'eager' and the cache is empty, with no sliding_window consideration; masking.py:226-227 propagates that None out of vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask. Direct call check: with _attn_implementation='sdpa', sliding_window=4, inputs_embeds (1,12,8), attention_mask=None the function returns None, while the same config with 'eager' returns a mask whose last query row allows only keys [8,9,10,11] (correct 4-wide window). Full-model repro (transformers 5.16.1): tiny MistralForCausalLM, sliding_window=4, sdpa, input (2,12). Upstream logits are identical with and without an all-ones mask (0.0) -- consistent with masking_utils.py:261-263 refusing the skip when 'local_attention_size is not None and kv_length >= local_attention_size'. After apply_transformers_model_patches(model, eager_attention=True) the patched model matches upstream exactly with a mask (0.0) but deviates by 0.158 max-abs without one (reporter's 0.39 was a different random config; same defect). Reachability: components/masking.py installs the shim in every registered family module, and DPTrainer keeps SDPA on CUDA/CPU (only _workaround_mps_bf16_sdpa forces eager, bf16+MPS only). The opaque SFT collator always emits attention_mask (sft/collator/_language_modeling.py), so opaque-collated training is safe, but DPTrainer passes batches through as-is and explicitly tolerates missing attention_mask (_dp_trainer.py:1809, 1827), so pre-packed datasets and any plain model(input_ids) eval/prefill call hit it. No test covers it: every sliding-window case in tests/transformers/runtime/test_masking.py uses _attn_implementation='eager' (lines 115, 119, 125, 215). Utility/correctness only, no sensitivity or accounting impact. Not a duplicate: #330 (parity tracker) was closed completed 2026-08-27, after the snapshot, and this is a live code defect in masking.py.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A patched sliding-window family (Mistral/Ministral, Gemma2, Gemma3 text, Cohere2, Phi-3) runs with attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default) and no attention_mask, on a prefill/no-cache call with seq_len >= sliding_window: vmap_create_causal_mask returns None, vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask forwards the None, SDPA falls back to is_causal=True, and sliding layers attend to the entire context instead of the last sliding_window tokens. Verified on tiny Mistral (sliding_window=4, seq=12, sdpa): patched no-mask logits differ from upstream by 0.158 max-abs while the masked path matches upstream bit-for-bit. Reachable from plain model(input_ids) eval/perplexity/generation-prefill code and from DPTrainer when the batch carries no attention_mask (pre-packed datasets); the opaque SFT collator always emits one, so its own flows are unaffected. Privacy accounting is untouched -- the harm is silently training/evaluating a model whose attention pattern differs from the architecture it claims to implement.

survivors.title: #495 quietly reverted #493's fail-closed dropout/batchify contract for default (trainer) calls
survivors.claim: Issue #400's fix (6e26cc97) made apply_transformers_model_patches raise for an unregistered family whenever dropout/batchify would apply, including via the compat=True default. Commit 2b309916 — titled 'fix(ci): separate Python and Rust test gates' — changed the guard to raise only when dropout/batchify was explicitly passed ('(dropout_explicit and dropout) or (batchify_explicit and batchify)'), so the default path silently skips both again with only a debug-level log, which is the pre-audit fail-open behavior. DPTrainer hits exactly this path: _dp_trainer.py:802-808 calls apply_model_patches(model, compat=True, ...) without explicit dropout/batchify kwargs, and its docstring (:791-793) still claims an 'info-level message' is logged.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user trains an unregistered-family HF model through DPTrainer with defaults: no exception, dropout modules keep p>0, and vmap(grad) runs with randomness='same' (_clipped_fun.py:310), so dropout noise is silently shared across all examples in the batch — gradients differ from both standard training and the dropout-free DP-SGD configuration the trainer documents, with only a debug log as signal. Privacy is unaffected (clipping still bounds sensitivity) but training numerics silently deviate.

verification.title: #495 quietly reverted #493's fail-closed dropout/batchify contract for default (trainer) calls
verification.reasoning: Every factual claim checks out, but the framing overstates the harm. Git history: 6e26cc97 (#493) introduced 'if dropout or batchify: raise ValueError' on the unregistered-family path; 2b309916 ('fix(ci): separate Python and Rust test gates ... (#495)') added dropout_explicit/batchify_explicit and narrowed the raise to '(dropout_explicit and dropout) or (batchify_explicit and batchify)' -- the diff really is inside a CI-titled commit that also touched two TRL compat tests. Current code is _router.py:116-135 as cited. Behaviour reproduced: a tiny FalconForCausalLM (unregistered) through apply_model_patches(m) with defaults raises nothing, logs only DEBUG 'no registered apply function for model family falcon', and leaves nn.Dropout p=0.3 untouched. DPTrainer calls apply_model_patches with only compat/performance/kernels (_dp_trainer.py:802-808) so it takes this path, and its docstring still promises an 'info-level message' (:791-793) while the code logs debug. randomness='same' confirmed at packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:310. Downgraded to low because the relaxation was not a stealth removal of a needed guard: #493's version raised for ANY unregistered family under default compat=True, including the plain nn.Module / custom fixtures DPTrainer explicitly documents as supported in the same docstring. Residual defect is narrow -- an inconsistent contract for unregistered HF families plus a debug-vs-info log/doc mismatch. No privacy impact: per-example clipping still bounds sensitivity. Tests (tests/transformers/components/test_dropout.py:56-88) pin only the explicit-kwarg raise and a compat=False no-raise; the default path is untested. #400 is closed; nothing open covers it.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user trains an HF model of an unregistered family (e.g. Falcon) through DPTrainer with defaults: apply_model_patches returns silently after a debug-level log, no compat patches are applied, and the model's dropout stays enabled (verified: nn.Dropout p stays 0.3 on a tiny Falcon). Under vmap(grad) with randomness='same' the surviving dropout mask is shared across every example in the batch, so gradients differ from both standard training and the dropout-free configuration the trainer documents. Privacy is unaffected. The user-visible defects are the missing signal (debug, while DPTrainer's docstring promises info) and the inconsistent contract between the explicit and default kwarg paths -- not a plain revert, since raising on the default path would break the custom/non-HF nn.Module models DPTrainer documents as supported.

survivors.title: Parity suite's 'upstream' reference is contaminated by unreverted module-global patches after the first test per family
survivors.claim: parity_model_patches (the #404 harness's isolation mechanism) snapshots and restores only class-level forward methods, but apply_transformers_model_patches also rebinds module-level globals via the family apply functions — mod.eager_attention_forward, mod.create_causal_mask/create_sliding_window_causal_mask, and ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS['sdpa'] — none of which are restored in the finally block. After the first parity test touches a family module, every later 'unpatched' reference model of that family in the same pytest process runs with opaque's attention and masking functions, so backward-grad, vmap-grad, sliding-window, softcapping and KV-cache parity assertions largely compare patched against patched.
survivors.failure_scenario: A future regression in vmap_eager_attention_forward or the mask builders that changes numerics identically for 'reference' and 'patched' models (because both use the patched module globals) passes the entire parity suite except the single first forward-logits test per family; the suite's claimed upstream-parity guarantee (closed #404, open #330) is materially weaker than stated. Empirically verified: after 'with parity_model_patches(patched): pass', modeling_llama.eager_attention_forward and modeling_llama.create_causal_mask are still the opaque replacements.

Every subsequent 'unpatched' reference model of that family therefore runs opaque's attention and mask builders, so the backward-grad, vmap-grad, sliding-window, softcapping and KV-cache comparisons -- and the entire eager attn_impl lane -- largely compare patched against patched. survivors.title: Gemma2 SDPA shim is installed in the process-global attention registry, rerouting every model family
survivors.claim: The #398 fix installs vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 via mod.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS['sdpa'] = ..., but ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS is one shared GeneralInterface instance across all transformers modeling modules (its __setitem__ writes the singleton's _local_mapping), so applying Gemma2 family patches reroutes SDPA attention for every model in the process. Empirically verified: after apply_gemma2_family_patches(), modeling_llama.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS['sdpa'] is vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2. For softcap=None callers the shim delegates verbatim to stock sdpa_attention_forward, but transformers 5.16 has other families that pass softcap to the interface (vaultgemma, t5gemma, videoprism) — for those, an unpatched model in the same process is silently switched to opaque's Gemma2 eager-attention math (softcap applied, eager instead of SDPA kernels) whereas upstream SDPA ignores softcap.
survivors.failure_scenario: A user patches a Gemma2 policy model, then loads an unpatched VaultGemma or T5Gemma reference/reward model in the same process with SDPA: its attention silently runs opaque's eager Gemma2 path — different numerics from upstream SDPA (softcap now applied), different speed/memory, attn_weights materialized — the same unscoped-global-override defect class issue #396 was filed about. Mirrors the audit's scoping concern rather than corrupting the patched model itself.

survivors.title: Fused activation backward still mutates saved gate/up activations in place (residual of #401/#402 pattern)
survivors.claim: The #482 fix removed the dX/X-storage reuse, but the fused LoRA MLP backward (and the standalone Opaque_SwiGLU/GeGLU backwards) still overwrite the autograd-saved gate/up activation tensors in place: _lora_mlp_backward_impl calls act_backward_fused(dh, gate_flat, up_flat) where gate_flat/up_flat are reshape views of ctx.saved_tensors, and _SwiGLUBackward.forward passes gate_flat/up_flat as both input and output pointers to the Triton kernel (swiglu.py:145-160, 'In-place: gate_flat → grad_gate, up_flat → grad_up'). The Triton write bypasses the dispatcher, so the tensor version counter is not bumped and autograd raises no error.
survivors.failure_scenario: loss.backward(retain_graph=True) followed by a second backward through the same graph (or any caller holding a reference to the gate/up tensors) silently computes the second pass from gradient values instead of activations — wrong gradients with no exception. The DP-SGD vmap(grad) path rebuilds the graph per call and is unaffected; double backward already raises NotImplementedError, but retain_graph re-traversal does not.

Not reached by opaque's own DP-SGD path (fresh graph per vmap(grad) call, gate/up discarded by the PEFT MLP forward, no retain_graph use anywhere in the tree); the numerical consequence was not executed here because the environment has no CUDA.

survivors.title: _mu_at hang fix is symptom-level: strong attacks with >2000 canary guesses now raise RuntimeError, including the default epsilon_at surface at the documented 10000-canary scale
survivors.claim: Commit 611faf51 (PR #299) fixes the infinite _mu_at hang by capping bracket doublings at 60 and raising RuntimeError — verified terminating in <1 s on the audit's pathological inputs (r=3000/u=0, r=5000/u=1400) — but it does not fix the underlying invariant (truncated ranks use v_k=0.5 regardless of mu at _gdp.py:333, so the Chernoff floor is n_trunc/2 and the p-value cannot rise above significance for any finite mu once u is well below n_trunc/2). Consequently every strong attack past _MAX_EXACT_RANKS=2000 guesses crashes instead of reporting an epsilon estimate.
survivors.failure_scenario: A practitioner audits with m=10000 canaries — the scale the user guide's own canary-count table discusses — and the mechanism is badly under-noised, so the attack reaches 62% accuracy (u=3800). Measured in this session: OneRunEstimate.epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) (the DEFAULT dispatch, which routes to gdp() at _estimate.py:197) raises 'RuntimeError: cannot invert μ-GDP p-value for (m=10000, r=10000, u=3800)...' while u=3900 (61% accuracy) still returns mu=2.23. The audit's most alarming regime — exactly what auditing exists to detect — becomes a crash whose message suggests using fewer canaries; nothing in docs/user-guide/auditing.md or docs/reference/auditing.md mentions the 2000-rank truncation or this failure mode (grep for '2000|truncat' returns nothing). Fail-closed, so no wrong epsilon is emitted, but the limitation is undocumented and the root-cause fix the original audit proposed (a mu-dependent v_k bound for truncated ranks) was not implemented.

Session experiment: GdpMethod stub (5000,5000): u=3800 → RuntimeError; u=3900 → mu=2.2311; u=3950 → mu=1.6210
Termination verified: (1500,1500,u=0) RuntimeError in 0.6 s; (2500,2500,u=1400) in 0.7 s; boundary case (1000,1000,u=0), r=2000, converges to mu=5.98/eps=42.6 in 18 s at the default grid

docs/user-guide/auditing.md:215-228 discusses canary counts up to 1,000,000 with no mention of the mu-GDP 2000-guess power cap; AUDIT-master-list.md:299 records the audit's proposed root-cause fix ('fixing the μ-dependent v_k bound resolves two of them')

survivors.title: fold_in's documented int/str domain disjointness is not structural: a 16-byte string collides with an integer fold
survivors.claim: The #374/#728 RNG convention rests on the docstring guarantee that 'Integers and strings are hashed down disjoint paths ... no sequence of integer folds can reach a key derived through a string fold' (_engine.py:64-67), but _stable_hash64 encodes an int as exactly its 16-byte signed little-endian form plus a '|' separator and a str as its UTF-8 bytes plus '|' with no type tag, so any string whose UTF-8 encoding equals the 16-byte encoding of an int produces the identical key. Demonstrated in this session: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed == fold_in(key(42), "\\x01" + "\\x00"*15).seed is True.
survivors.failure_scenario: All of Opaque's own stream roots are dotted-ASCII tags whose lengths differ from 16 bytes, so no internal stream collides today (the test_stream_root_namespacing.py guarantees hold). The exposure is the same forward-looking class OPQ-128 warned about: a third-party mechanism or future internal tag that happens to be a 16-byte string containing bytes aliasing a caller-integer fold would silently share a stream with an integer derivation, and the documented invariant users are told to rely on would not hold. No current epsilon is affected.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:27-35 (_stable_hash64: int → to_bytes(16,'little',signed=True)+b'|', str → utf-8+b'|', no type discriminator)
Session repro: fold_in(key(42), 1) == fold_in(key(42), '\\x01'+'\\x00'*15) → True, contradicting _engine.py:64-65

packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py only probes integer folds in range(-64,512) and split(base,16) against the actual internal tags, so it cannot catch the encoding-aliasing class
survivors.fix_sketch: Prefix a one-byte type tag in _stable_hash64 (e.g. b'i' before int bytes, b's' before str bytes) — a breaking key-derivation change like #728 itself, or soften the docstring to state the separation is encoding-based and NUL-containing 16-byte strings are reserved.

verification.title: fold_in's documented int/str domain disjointness is not structural: a 16-byte string collides with an integer fold
verification.reasoning: Reproduced. _engine.py:27-35 _stable_hash64 encodes an int as to_bytes(16, 'little', signed=True) + b'|' and any other value as str(part).encode('utf-8') + b'|', with no type discriminator, so the two paths share one byte stream. Executed: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed == fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15).seed -> both 2142789487919306769, True. That directly contradicts the docstring at :64-67 ('Integers and strings are hashed down disjoint paths ... no sequence of integer folds can reach a key derived through a string fold'), which the whole documented RNG convention rests on. Severity held at low and I would not raise it: reachability is essentially nil in practice. Colliding with a small caller integer (step, rank, leaf index) requires a string whose UTF-8 encoding is 15 NUL bytes plus one payload byte; colliding with a printable 16-byte ASCII tag requires the caller to fold an integer around 10^38, which nothing in Opaque does. Every internal stream root is a dotted-ASCII tag of non-16-byte length, so no current stream collides, and no epsilon is affected. The real defect is that a documented invariant users are told to rely on is enforced by convention rather than by encoding. Nothing in the open-issue snapshot covers it (#374 is closed).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: The docstring invariant at _engine.py:64-67 is false as written: because _stable_hash64 tags neither ints nor strs, fold_in(key(42), 1) and fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15) produce byte-identical keys (verified). The practical exposure is negligible -- a colliding string must encode to exactly 16 bytes matching the little-endian signed image of a folded integer, which for the small integers Opaque folds means a string of NUL bytes, and for a printable ASCII tag would require folding an integer near 10^38. No Opaque stream root collides today and no epsilon changes. The residual risk is that a third-party mechanism relying on the stated guarantee has no structural protection behind it; the fix is a one-byte type discriminator in _stable_hash64, or weakening the docstring claim.

survivors.title: mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' pairs a plain Poisson sampler with cyclic-Poisson horizon accounting, underreporting epsilon
survivors.claim: TrainingArguments explicitly allows privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' with sampling_mode='poisson' (_training_arguments.py:188 `"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})`, comment :182 calls it a 'looser-but-valid alternative'), but for that mode build_amplifier_factory constructs the CyclicPoisson horizon accountant (`_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), sample_rate, n_steps)`, _dpftrl.py:140-154) while build_sampler constructs the plain DP-SGD `PoissonSampler` (_dpftrl.py:224-233, imported from opaque.dpsgd.sampling), not the `CyclicPoissonSampler` the accountant's analysis requires. CyclicPoisson.pld_at charges only `num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands)` compositions of a Poisson-Gaussian at per-participation sensitivity 1 (_poisson.py:179-188, 214), which is the amplified-BandMF reduction (Choquette-Choo et al. 2023, arXiv:2306.08153) valid only when each example can participate in at most one step per bands-wide window (the cyclic group scheme). Plain Poisson samples every example independently at every one of the n steps (dpsgd/_poisson.py:33-38), so a record participates ~Binomial(n, q) times with no separation guarantee — both the composition count (n/bands vs ~n effective) and the per-window sensitivity assumption are violated. Both mid-run epsilon_at (via per_step -> pld_at(K), _dp_trainer.py:1766, 3960) and noise-multiplier calibration (_dp_trainer.py:4222-4237) use this accountant, so the run is calibrated against and reports an epsilon that does not bound the deployed mechanism.
survivors.failure_scenario: User sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' (bands=16 default), sampling_mode='poisson' (passes validation at _training_arguments.py:1048), n=1600 steps, q=0.01, target eps=1. Calibration sizes nm so that ceil(1600/16)=100 Poisson-Gaussian compositions hit eps=1; the deployed run actually gives each record ~16 expected participations across all 1600 steps with possible same-band-window repeats. Measured reference: 100 compositions of poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01) give eps(1e-6)=0.954 while the 1600-composition independent-noise reference gives 2.649 — the true epsilon of the deployed banded mechanism under plain Poisson is at least on that order, so the reported/calibrated epsilon is ~2.8x too small at bands=16 and grows with bands. Silent: no warning, training completes, accountant.json records the invalid bound.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:182-188 — '# ``mf_band`` accepts ``"poisson"`` as a looser-but-valid alternative to' ... '"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})'; validation at :1048 only checks membership in this set.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:138-154 — sampling_mode=='poisson' returns `_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, _s), sample_rate=_sr, n_steps=_ns, ...)` with _s = the BandMfStrategy; _dpftrl.py:224-233 — same mode returns `PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=sample_rate, ...)`.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:179-188,214 — BandMF branch: `rounded = min(-(-n_steps // bands) * bands, self.n_steps); num_groups = math.ceil(rounded / bands)` then `per_group_pld.self_compose(num_groups)`; module docstring :3-7 states the analysis divides the run into ceil(n_steps/bands) independent groups — a property of the cyclic scheme, not of plain Poisson.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:43-56 — CyclicPoissonSampler is the sampler implementing the accounted scheme ('Step i samples only from group i % bands'); build_sampler only constructs it for sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson', which is NOT in _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS for any mechanism.

Measured (this session): (poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01)*100).epsilon_at(1e-6)=0.9542 vs (*1600)=2.6495; BandMfStrategy.sensitivity(n_steps=N)=1.0 exactly (coefficients L2-normalized in _toeplitz.py optimize), so effective_nm == nm and the accountant is exactly the 100-fold composition.

verification.title: mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' pairs a plain Poisson sampler with cyclic-Poisson horizon accounting, underreporting epsilon
verification.reasoning: Every link verified. (1) Config: _training_arguments.py:188 '"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})', validation at :1048 only checks membership, test_config.py:549 test_mf_band_accepts_poisson_override pins it, and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:142 advertises 'b_min_sep (or explicit poisson)'. (2) Accounting: _dpftrl.py:138-154 builds _ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), ...) -> CyclicPoisson, whose pld_at (dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:178-214) computes num_groups = ceil(rounded/bands) and returns poisson_gaussian_pld(nm/sensitivity, q).self_compose(num_groups). BandMfStrategy.sensitivity (_band_mf.py:128-130) ignores min_sep/max_participations and returns the coefficient column norm; measured exactly 1.0 at n_steps=1600, bands=16, so the accountant is literally the ceil(n/bands)-fold Poisson-Gaussian composition (measured eps(1e-6)=0.9542 at nm=1, q=0.01, n=1600, bands=16, identical to repeat(poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01),100)). (3) Runtime: _dpftrl.py:224-233 returns PoissonSampler from opaque.dpsgd.sampling (independent Bernoulli(q) over the whole dataset every step); the matching CyclicPoissonSampler is only built for sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson', which no mechanism allows. (4) Both feed the run: _dp_trainer.py:1467 builds the amplifier from the same a.sampling_mode used at :3704 for the sampler, and :4227 wraps it for calibration and epsilon reporting. The ceil(n/bands) reduction is the amplified-BandMF result (Choquette-Choo et al. 2023), valid only under one participation per bands-wide window; under plain Poisson the per-window inclusion probability is 1-(1-q)^bands, not q. Already at bands=2, n=2 the deployed mixture puts mass 1-(1-q)^2 on a nonzero shift while the accountant charges only q, so it is provably not an upper bound. Not tracked: #699/#697 are prefix-tightening (and closed upstream), #356/#320 ('a mismatch between runtime and accounting raises before training') are closed as completed, and open #359 is about BandMfStrategy.sensitivity being participation-blind — this is the concrete shipped end-to-end pairing plus a composition-count mismatch (n/bands vs n) that #359 never mentions, i.e. a materially worse instance rather than a duplicate.
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' with the documented sampling_mode='poisson' override (bands=16 default). The accountant charges ceil(n_steps/bands) compositions of a Poisson-Gaussian at per-participation sensitivity 1 — the cyclic-group reduction — while the deployed sampler draws every example independently at every step with no band separation. At nm=1, q=0.01, n=1600, bands=16 the reported and calibrated eps(1e-6) is 0.954; the identity-sampling reference over the same 1600 steps is 2.65 and a per-band-window-rate reference (100 groups at rate 1-(1-q)^16=0.148) is 12.0, so the reported epsilon understates the deployed mechanism by at least ~2.8x and likely far more, growing with bands. No warning is emitted; training completes and the accountant record stores the invalid bound.

survivors.title: BallsInBins.pld_at docstring claims K-epoch reparameterization for BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD and carries an unreachable BLT pinned-prefix gram branch
survivors.claim: The pld_at docstring (:150-152) states 'For horizon-independent inners (Identity, BSR, BiSR, lambda-CGD) the gram / primitive is reparameterised by K_epochs' and describes an N-pinned BLT prefix gram (:152-156), but the guard at :181 (`if not isinstance(s, IdentityStrategy) and rounded < self.n_steps: return self.pld_at(self.n_steps, ...)`) snaps EVERY non-Identity prefix to the full-horizon PLD. The BLT pinned-coefficient branch (:216-235) and the BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD `gram_matrix(n_steps=rounded)` branch (:236-244) therefore only execute with rounded == self.n_steps, where they reproduce the full-horizon gram — the prefix differentiation is dead code, and the docstring contradicts its own last two sentences (:156-158, 'Correlated-strategy Monte Carlo paths use the full-horizon confidence bound for every nonzero prefix'). Behavior is conservative (full-horizon PLD dominates any prefix by post-processing over the causal streaming transcript), so this is a maintenance trap, not a privacy defect.
survivors.failure_scenario: A contributor implementing open issues #694/#696/#698/#700 reads :150-156, concludes the K-epoch gram path is already live and tested, and deletes the :181 guard — activating the never-exercised gram-at-rounded path (including the BLT coefs[:rounded] slice whose validity as a bound for K < N was never established) with no test able to catch it, since no test currently reaches those branches with rounded < n_steps.
evidence: _balls_in_bins.py:181-191 — early return to pld_at(self.n_steps) for every non-Identity strategy with rounded < n_steps.
_balls_in_bins.py:216-235 — `if isinstance(s, BltStrategy): ... pinned = list(coefs[:rounded].tolist())` — only reachable when rounded == self.n_steps, so coefs[:rounded] is always the whole column.
_balls_in_bins.py:150-152 vs :156-158 — the same docstring asserts both K-epoch reparameterization and full-horizon-for-every-prefix.
Open issues #694/#696/#698/#700 track tightening these prefixes; the in-code self-contradiction and dead differentiation are not mentioned in any open issue title.
survivors.fix_sketch: Rewrite the pld_at docstring to describe shipped behavior only (Identity: exact per-epoch prefix; everything else: full-horizon bound), and either delete the dead BLT/BSR prefix-gram differentiation or gate it behind the tightening work with tests that actually reach it.

survivors.title: accounting.md documents a 'hypergeometric prefix mixture' for k_out_of_t that the Python surface never computes
survivors.claim: docs/user-guide/accounting.md:180-183 states for `dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t`: 'pld_at(K) accounts the hypergeometric prefix mixture; the full k>1 PLD uses the conservative Feldman-Shenfeld block reduction.' survivors.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture; the #748 confidence bound certifies the wrong functional and the add-direction PLD is anti-conservative
survivors.claim: likelihood_ratio_warm computes `sum_f = f[0] + p*tail/denom` (denom = 1+(b-1)p), i.e. it divides only the barred-start terms by the warm-start normalizer while leaving f[0] undivided. The code's own remove-direction sampler `sample_x_under_p` (mc.rs:85-108) draws the initial barred state from the stationary distribution P(state 0)=1/denom, P(state j)=p/denom, whose exact density ratio is (f[0] + p*sum_{j=1}^{b-1} f[j])/denom. The coded expression is therefore not the likelihood ratio of ANY initial-state mixture (its E_Q would need weights summing to 1+(b-1)p/denom > 1). Consequently the Monte Carlo 'privacy loss' samples fed into the PR #748 confidence-band machinery (samples_to_pmf) are ln of an inflated statistic, not the true log-likelihood ratio: the remove-direction PLD is inflated (still an upper bound, but systematically loose by up to ~ln(1+(b-1)p)), and the add-direction PLD is shifted DOWN, so the add-direction epsilon/delta certificate is invalid (underestimates the true add-direction hockey-stick). The final epsilon = max(remove, add); when the deflated add side binds (possible after composing the asymmetric MC PLD with other mechanisms, or in configs where add dominates), the reported 'high-confidence bound' understates the true epsilon. This is reachable from the public API via opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/__init__.py:191-214 calls _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld / bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle), and the July audit's closed issue #337 ('Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification', claimed fixed by #748) is therefore incompletely fixed on this path. The runtime BMinSepSampler also uses the stationary warm start (July audit master list line 158 verified P(eligible)=1/(1+(b-1)p)), so the accountant's functional mismatches the deployed mechanism, not just its own internal sampler. The bug predates the audit (introduced in commit 5de05eb0, PR #121) and survived both the audit and PR #748, which rewrote the surrounding sample-to-PMF pipeline without touching these four lines. Distinct from open issue #697 (prefix tightness / MC-error certification): this is a wrong likelihood-ratio functional, not an uncertified error.
survivors.failure_scenario: User configures BandMF with b-min-sep sampling, e.g. bands=2, p=0.05, n=50, sigma=1.0 (the repo's own mc_pld_smoke configuration). Faithful Python reimplementation of the Rust code (verified line-by-line against mc.rs:25-76): E_Q[r_code] = 1.16647 +/- 0.003 vs required 1.0 (analytic prediction 1+(b-1)p/denom = 1.16667 at p=0.2); importance-sampling identity P[ln r > t] = E_Q[r*1{ln r>t}] fails for the coded r (0.4597 vs 0.5366 at t=0.5) and holds for the corrected r (0.3939 vs 0.3939). Epsilon impact at delta=0.01 (plain-MC hockey stick, 60k samples): CODE eps_remove=1.286 / eps_add=0.720 vs TRUE eps_remove=1.239 / eps_add=0.766 -- the standalone reported max is inflated ~4% (silent over-noising after calibration), and the add-direction certificate underestimates the true add epsilon by ~6%; with larger bands*p (e.g. bands=32, p=0.02, denom=1.62) the remove inflation grows toward ln(1.62)~0.48 whole-run epsilon while the add deficit grows symmetrically. In any composition where the add adjacency binds the composed maximum, the returned '1-mc_failure_probability confidence' epsilon is below the true epsilon: silent privacy loss.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:69-75: `let denom = 1.0 + (bands.saturating_sub(1) as f64) * p; let mut sum_f = f[0]; if bands > 1 { let tail: f64 = (1..bands).map(|j| f[j]).sum::<f64>(); sum_f += p * tail / denom; } sum_f` -- f[0] is not divided by denom.

Numerical check (scratchpad/check_lr_warm.py, faithful reimplementation, numpy 2.1.3): E_Q[r_code]=1.16647 (se 0.003) vs analytic 1+(b-1)p/denom=1.16667; E_Q[r_true]=0.99982. IS-consistency holds only for the corrected formula (t=0.5: TRUE 0.3939 vs 0.3939; CODE 0.4597 vs 0.5366).

Epsilon quantification (scratchpad/check_lr_eps.py): delta=0.01 -> CODE eps_remove=1.2858/eps_add=0.7195, TRUE eps_remove=1.2393/eps_add=0.7660; add-direction delta at eps=0.3: code 0.14870 vs true 0.19815 (25% underestimate).

verification.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture; the add-direction PLD is anti-conservative
verification.reasoning: The mathematical defect is confirmed independently and decisively. mc.rs:69-75 computes sum_f = f[0] + p*sum_{j=1}^{b-1} f[j]/denom with denom = 1+(b-1)p, dividing only the barred-start terms. The module's own sampler sample_x_under_p (mc.rs:85-108) starts in the stationary state (state 0 w.p. 1/denom, state j w.p. p/denom), whose exact density ratio is (f[0] + p*sum f[j])/denom. I wrote an independent exact enumeration of P(y)/Q(y) over all warm-start participation patterns (scratchpad/vfy_lr.py) and compared both formulas at bands=2,3, n=8..10: the corrected formula matches exact enumeration to ~1e-15 in every case, while the shipped formula overstates it by 1.048-1.171x (b=2,p=0.05 -> 1.0475; b=2,p=0.2 -> 1.164; b=3,p=0.1 -> 1.167). The shipped statistic is thus not the likelihood ratio of any initial-state mixture (E_Q = 1+(b-1)p/denom > 1; measured 1.046 and 1.227). Since r_code > r_true pointwise, ln(r) inflates the remove-direction PLD (conservative) and -ln(r) deflates the add-direction PLD (anti-conservative). Independent MC quantification (scratchpad/vfy_lr_eps.py, 200k/100k samples, delta=1e-2): repo smoke config (coef=[sqrt.7,sqrt.3], n=50, p=0.05) CODE remove 1.271 / add 0.719 vs TRUE 1.224 / 0.766; 16 equal bands, p=0.02 (denom=1.30) CODE 1.390 / 0.381 vs TRUE 1.178 / 0.585. Consumer check: PrivacyLossDistribution::epsilon_at returns the max over adjacencies (pld/mod.rs:266-293) and no Python API exposes the add side alone, so in every configuration I could construct the inflated remove side binds and the user-visible epsilon is over-stated by 4-18% — an error in the conservative direction (silent over-noising), not a privacy loss. The anti-conservative add component is real but latent: binding would require composing with a mechanism whose add-side asymmetry exceeds the ~0.6 remove-add gap, which I could not exhibit — hence high -> medium. Reachable from opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep, the default sampler for mf_band; no test compares bands>=2 output to any oracle. Not tracked (#697 closed and about MC-error certification; #359 about BandMF sensitivity; #666 about regression vectors).
verification.corrected_failure_scenario: Any BandMF + b-min-sep run (the default sampler for privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band') is priced with a statistic that is not the warm-start likelihood ratio: verified against exact enumeration, the shipped value exceeds the true P(y)/Q(y) by up to a factor denom = 1+(bands-1)p. Because epsilon_at takes the max over adjacencies and the inflated remove side bound in every test, the practical effect is an over-stated epsilon — 1.271 vs 1.224 at the repo's own smoke config, 1.390 vs 1.178 at 16 bands with p=0.02 (delta=1e-2) — so calibration picks a larger-than-necessary noise multiplier and utility is silently lost. The mirror-image deflation of the add-direction PLD (0.381 vs a true 0.585 in the 16-band config) makes that component an invalid bound; it is currently masked by the max but would understate epsilon in any composition where the add adjacency binds.

survivors.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo epsilon depends on Rayon thread count with a fixed seed -- the #331 reproducibility fix covered only balls-in-bins, not the sibling sampler PR #748 also touched
survivors.claim: Closed issue #331 ('Make balls-in-bins Monte Carlo reproducible across thread counts') was fixed by giving bnb_mc_pld fixed 1024-sample shards whose seeds depend only on the shard index (monte_carlo.rs:43-55: 'The shard count must depend only on the resolved sample count, not on the Rayon worker count: users expect a fixed seed to select the same samples on every machine'). The sibling MC sampler bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld -- rewritten by the same PR #748 for the confidence-bound plumbing -- still partitions its RNG streams by `rayon::current_num_threads()` and seeds per-thread StdRngs as seed+tid (remove) and seed+1000+tid (add), so the drawn sample set, and therefore the reported epsilon, changes with the machine's core count. bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (mc.rs:174-218) has the same dependence even though it runs serially (it deliberately mirrors the thread partition), so cached transcript corpora prepared on one machine differ from another; the Python transcript cache key (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/_transcript_cache.py:32 `key = (strategy_coef, n_steps, p, num_mc_samples, mc_seed)`) does not capture the thread count, so identical keys map to different corpora across environments. Reproducibility is a documented contract of `seed` ('RNG seed for Monte Carlo reproducibility', discretization.py:25/123) and the only regression test (tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py) covers balls-in-bins alone. Additionally, seed+1000+tid collides with the remove streams whenever current_num_threads() > 1000 (remove tid=1000 equals add tid=0), which would reuse identical randomness across adjacency directions on very large machines.
survivors.failure_scenario: Measured on this tree (RAYON_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,8}, seed=173, coef=[sqrt(0.7),sqrt(0.3)], n=50, p=0.05, sigma=1.0, mc_resolution=5e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-2): epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.5789 (1 thread), 1.5938 (2 threads), 1.8443 (8 threads) -- a 17% swing in the reported guarantee from the core count alone. A team pinning seed=42 in CI on a 4-core runner and deploying calibration on a 64-core box gets a different noise multiplier for the 'same' configuration; privacy statements citing a specific (epsilon, delta, seed) triple are not verifiable on other hardware. Each individual value is still a valid confidence bound for its own sample set (given finding 1 is fixed), so this is silent nondeterminism of the reported guarantee rather than an invalid bound.
